This is a documentation-only change that requires no testing.

author: josephsl
body:
One of the possibilities after #18220 merge:

### Link to issue number:
Closes #16862 
Closes #17384 

### Summary of the issue:
NVDA does not support Windows 11 Voice Access features including text dictation announcement from everywhere.

### Description of user facing changes:
Introduces support for Windows 11 Voice Access, including text dictation, microphone toggle announcement, and mouse and touch interaction. Requires NVDA to be installed.

### Description of developer facing changes:
Added voiceaccess.py app module, based on #18220 work.

### Description of development approach:
The new Voice Access app module includes:

* isGoodUIAWindow: says "yes" for "Voice Access" window class name (enables mouse and touch interaction)
* Should process UIA notification event says "yes" as Voice Access notification elements do not have native window handle
* UIA notification event will announce display string from everywhere.

### Testing strategy:
Manual and requires NVDA to be installed:

1. Enable and run Voice Access on Windows 11.
2. When Voice Access screen appears, try toggling microphone by saying "microphone sleep". Observe that NVDA announces toggle state of microphone.
3. Move to a text field (say, Notepad) and dictate text. Observe that NVDA echoes back dictated text.

### Known issues with pull request:
As Voice Access requires admin privileges, this app module will not work on portable and temporary (installer) copies of NVDA. This limitation is documented in the user guide as an example of an app with admin privileges. Further, as dictated text will be announced from everywhere, users should be advised to wear headphones when dictating (for privacy) unless the situation does allow echoing of text to be acceptable.

## Summary
- Fix 404 error when accessing entry detail pages in admin interface
- Properly handle the `/admin/entry/` URL prefix in path extraction

Entry detail pages were returning 404 errors because the path extraction logic only removed `/entry/` but didn't account for the React Router `basename="/admin"` configuration, resulting in incorrect paths being sent to the API.

Updated `AdminEntryPage.tsx` to correctly parse paths from URLs like `/admin/entry/some-path` by removing both `/admin/entry/` and `/entry/` prefixes.

author: flooie
body:
Find Citations was silently failing for a handful of reasons.

The retry function was passing kwargs - which appears to need the retry to use position arguments.
This was causing a TypeError and failing retries.  Additionally, this may have been swallowing up 
the error that was causing the retry.  

Now instead, we are logging directly into sentry the specific opinion that failed and why.  This should 
open up our error failing in eyecite.  

Additionally, we are checking for self references, and in opinions where no opinions have been found we 
were causing a bug.  Now we return no match resources if the count remains 0

body:
In this pull request, we allow dmypy suggest absolute paths to contain the drive letter colon for Windows machines. Fixes #19335.

<!-- If this pull request fixes an issue, add "Fixes #NNN" with the issue number. -->

This is done by changing how `find_node` works slightly, allowing there to be at most two colon (`:`) characters in the passed key for windows machines instead of just one like on all other platforms, and then using `rsplit` and a split limit of 1 instead of just `split` like prior.

I was looking at the existing tests for dmypy suggest and noticed nothing is testing absolute paths for any platform, so I am unsure what I need to do to add tests; This sounds like maybe it could require changes to the test framework system, and I'd like feedback from others before trying to do that.

##### Semver-minor features

##### 🔧 `fs.FileHandle.readableWebStream` gets `autoClose` option

This gives developers explicit control over whether the file descriptor should
be closed when the stream ends. Helps avoid subtle resource leaks.

Contributed by James M Snell in [#​58548](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58548).

##### 🔧 `fs.Dir` now supports **explicit resource management**

This improves ergonomics around async iteration of directories. Developers can
now manually control when a directory is closed using `.close()` or with `Symbol.asyncDispose`.

Contributed by Antoine du Hamel in [#​58206](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58206).

##### 📊 `http2` gains diagnostics channel: `http2.server.stream.finish`

Adds observability support for when a stream finishes. Useful for logging,
monitoring, and debugging HTTP/2 behavior without patching internals.

Contributed by Darshan Sen in [#​58560](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58560).

##### 🔐 Permissions: implicit allow-fs-read to entrypoint

Node.js permissions model now allows read access to the entry file by default.
It makes running permission-restricted apps smoother while preserving security.

Contributed by Rafael Gonzaga in [#​58579](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58579).

inherited terminal styles when composing styled strings.

body:
This PR implements comprehensive support for AirplaneEntities, mirroring the existing AutomobileEntity functionality to provide consistent character interaction capabilities.

## Changes Made

### Character Placement
- Added `MW_Player_ThirdPerson_PlaceCharacterInAirplaneEntity()` function that places characters inside airplane entities
- Implemented `MW_Input_EnvMod_PlaceCharacterInAirplane()` to handle airplane interaction input
- Characters can now enter airplanes via right-click and grip interactions in HAND mode

### Entity Creation and Loading
- Added AirplaneEntity creation support in `MW_Entity_LoadEntity()` for both placing and placed modes
- Implemented proper Physical interaction state for airplanes in both entity loading and placement systems
- Airplanes now behave consistently with automobiles regarding physics and interactions

### Exit Functionality
- The existing `MW_Player_ThirdPerson_ExitVehicle()` function already works generically for all vehicle types
- Characters can exit airplanes using the same mechanism as automobiles

### Delete Functionality
- Enhanced SLEDGE-HAMMER interaction mode to support deleting airplane entities
- Airplanes can now be removed from the world using destruction tools

## Implementation Details

The implementation follows the established AutomobileEntity pattern for consistency:

```javascript
// Character placement mirrors automobile logic
function MW_Player_ThirdPerson_PlaceCharacterInAirplaneEntity(airplaneEntity) {
    var context = Context.GetContext("THIRD_PERSON_CHARACTER_CONTROLLER");
    context.characterEntity.SetParent(airplaneEntity);
    context.characterEntity.SetPosition(new Vector3(0, 1, -4), true, false);
    // ... additional setup identical to automobiles
    context.inVehicle = true;
    context.activeVehicle = airplaneEntity;
}
```

```javascript
// Entity creation follows established pattern
else if (type == "airplane") {
    AirplaneEntity.Create(parentEntity, modelPath, [ modelPath ], offset, rotation,
        mass, null, null, "MW_Entity_FinishLoadingPlacingEntity");
}
```

## Testing

All functionality has been validated through comprehensive testing:
- ✅ Character placement in airplanes works correctly
- ✅ Character exit functionality works generically for all vehicles
- ✅ Airplane entity creation and loading functions properly
- ✅ Delete functionality includes airplane support
- ✅ All interaction modes handle airplanes appropriately
- ✅ Implementation maintains consistency with automobile patterns

The changes provide complete feature parity between AutomobileEntity and AirplaneEntity support, ensuring users can interact with airplane entities in exactly the same way as automobile entities.

Fixes #6.

author: ypatil12
body:
**Motivation:**

We need deploy scripts for multichain 

**Modifications:**

Adds a `crossChainDeployLib` from: https://github.com/Layr-Labs/eigenlayer-contracts/pull/1474. This library uses `createX` for deterministic deployments. In order to keep the same address on all `destinationChains`, we deploy contracts from the same multisig on each chain. 

Add `testnet-base-sepolia` to CI for deploy scripts. 

Adds a `deploy_globalRootConfirmerSet` script. This script initiates a global root confirmer set (ie. generator) and updates the `network.toml` file used in the deploy scripts. It is only intended to be used on `preprod` and `testnet`. 

To distinguish between a source and destination chain we add a `SOURCE_CHAIN: bool` and `DESTINATION_CHAIN: bool` to the Zeus Config. We skip parts of the deploy if a chain is not a source or destination. 

Deploys the contracts in 5 steps

1. `deploySourceChain.s.sol`: Deploys `KeyRegistrar`, `ReleaseManager`, `CrossChainRegistry`. 
2. `deployDestinationChainProxies.s.sol`: Deploys _empty_ proxy contracts for `OperatorTableUpdater`, `BN254CertificateVerifier`, `ECDSACertificateVerifier`. _Note: in order to have deterministic proxies, we need to ensure the `initCode` is the same. Thus, the implementation is the same `emptyContract` and the proxyAdmin is initially the `multichainDeployerMultisig`_. 
3. `deployDestinationChainImpls`: Deploys implementations using EOA
4. `instantiateDestinationChainProxies`: Upgrades the proxies to the actual implementations. Transfer proxy admin to the actual `proxyAdmin`
5. `configureCrossChainRegistry`: Updates the `crossChainRegistry` on the `SOURCE_CHAIN` to whitelist proper chainIds

**Result:**

Deploy scripts

**Issue:** #4347

### Description

There is an issue when you switch from a model where the thinking budget is very high to a model where that thinking budget is greater than the max_output of the new model. This results in the provider keeping the old value of the thinking budget which is higher then the new max_output of the model. This results in the llm api request erroring out

The fix done here is to set max_output as thinking_budget - 1 if there is an issue with these numbers.

author: waefrebeorn
body:
When CFG is active and no audio prefix codes are provided, the Zonos model expects the `prefix_conditioning` tensor to have an even batch size (representing concatenated conditional and unconditional parts).

The `synthesize_to_bytes` method in `ZonosLocalVoice` was previously only preparing a single conditional part, leading to an odd batch size (e.g., 1) for `prefix_conditioning`.

This commit modifies `synthesize_to_bytes` to:
1. Detect if CFG is active based on `cfg_scale`.
2. If active, create parameters for an unconditional pass by nullifying keys specified in `unconditional_keys_cfg` (e.g., speaker, emotion).
3. Call `make_cond_dict` for both conditional and unconditional parameters.
4. Pass both resulting dictionaries to `Zonos.prepare_conditioning`.

This ensures `prefix_conditioning` has the correct doubled batch size for CFG, resolving the `ValueError` in `Zonos.generate`.

# 🔒 Enhanced Nested Pickle Detection with Security Hardening

## 📋 Summary

This PR implements robust nested pickle detection capabilities to identify multi-stage serialization attacks and hidden malicious payloads within pickle files. The implementation includes comprehensive security hardening, performance optimizations, and extensive testing to prevent false positives.

## 🛡️ Security Enhancements

### **Critical Bug Fixes**
- **Fixed major false positive bug** in `_looks_like_pickle()` that incorrectly identified random text as pickle data
- **Fixed undefined variable error** in decode-exec chain detection
- **Improved regex validation** to prevent false positives on legitimate model data

### **New Security Features**
- **Nested pickle detection**: Identifies pickle payloads embedded within other pickle files
- **Encoded payload detection**: Detects base64/hex-encoded pickle data hiding malicious content  
- **Decode-exec chain detection**: Identifies patterns like `base64.decode` → `pickle.loads/eval`

4. If the PR is unfinished, see how to mark it: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/guide/pull-requests.md#marking-unfinished-pull-requests
-->

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
Updates the way that the server discovers valid partitions and regions during token verification. In essence, the host of a token is valid if it 1) comes from the same partition as the server and 2) contains a valid region.

Functionality changes
* This weakens the verification check, as it does not check that host regions are supported by STS. 

Implementation changes
* Listing partitions through the  `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/aws/endpoints` package → using a hardcoded list of partitions
* Discovering regions through the `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go/aws/endpoints` package → discovering regions through the `ec2.DescribeRegions` API. 
    * The call yields all available regions to an account, regardless of opt-in status.

Testing
* Tested that the verify command still a) correctly verifies a token from the same partition and b) correctly denies tokens from different partitions

Created a token using credentials from an account in the `aws` partition (`US_TOKEN`) and an account in the `aws-cn` partition (`CHINA_TOKEN`)

Ran `verify` on each token using accounts from within their partition, one with the same and one with a different region than the account that created the token. I was able to see that the token was correctly successfully verified when an account is in the same partition as the one that generated the token, regardless of region.

Output of this test for `CHINA_TOKEN` (similar for `US_TOKEN`):
```
&{ARN:arn:aws-cn:sts::<account id>:assumed-role/Admin/<user> CanonicalARN:arn:aws-cn:iam::<account id>:role/<role> AccountID:<account id> UserID:<user-id> SessionName:<user> AccessKeyID:<access-key-id> STSEndpoint:sts.cn-northwest-1.amazonaws.com.cn}
```

Then, I ran `verify` on each token with both the correct and incorrect partition (`aws` for `CHINA_TOKEN` and `aws-cn` for `US_TOKEN`) to replicate conditions where the client is in a different partition from the server. I saw that the command correctly rejected the tokens when coming from a different partition.

Output for `US_TOKEN` (similar for `CHINA_TOKEN`):
```
# same partition (aws)
(25-06-24 23:47:21) <0> [/aws-iam-authenticator]
dev % /aws-iam-authenticator/_output/bin/aws-iam-authenticator verify —cluster-id=<id> —token=$US_TOKEN —partition=aws
[Warn] Region not found in instance metadata, err: operation error ec2imds: GetRegion, access disabled to EC2 IMDS via client option, or "AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED" environment variable
&{ARN:arn:aws:sts::<account-id>:assumed-role/admin/<role> CanonicalARN:arn:aws:iam::<account-id>:role/<role> AccountID:<account-id> UserID:<user-id> SessionName:<session-nmae> AccessKeyID:<key-id> STSEndpoint:sts.us-west-2.amazonaws.com}

# different partition (aws-cn)
(25-06-24 23:47:33) <0> [/aws-iam-authenticator]
dev % /aws-iam-authenticator/_output/bin/aws-iam-authenticator verify —cluster-id=<id> —token=$US_TOKEN —partition=aws-cn
[Warn] Region not found in instance metadata, err: operation error ec2imds: GetRegion, access disabled to EC2 IMDS via client option, or "AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED" environment variable
could not verify token: input token was not properly formatted: unexpected hostname "sts.us-west-2.amazonaws.com" in pre-signed URL
```
Note that the warning about ec2imds comes from the fact that the `AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED` env var is set to true, if set to false the output is the same but without the warning.

##### 🔧 `fs.FileHandle.readableWebStream` gets `autoClose` option

This gives developers explicit control over whether the file descriptor should
be closed when the stream ends. Helps avoid subtle resource leaks.

Contributed by James M Snell in [#​58548](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58548).

##### 🔧 `fs.Dir` now supports **explicit resource management**

This improves ergonomics around async iteration of directories. Developers can
now manually control when a directory is closed using `.close()` or with `Symbol.asyncDispose`.

Contributed by Antoine du Hamel in [#​58206](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58206).

##### 📊 `http2` gains diagnostics channel: `http2.server.stream.finish`

Adds observability support for when a stream finishes. Useful for logging,
monitoring, and debugging HTTP/2 behavior without patching internals.

Contributed by Darshan Sen in [#​58560](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58560).

##### 🔐 Permissions: implicit allow-fs-read to entrypoint

Node.js permissions model now allows read access to the entry file by default.
It makes running permission-restricted apps smoother while preserving security.

Contributed by Rafael Gonzaga in [#​58579](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58579).

##### 🎨 `util.styleText()` adds `'none'` style

This lets developers remove styling cleanly without hacks. Useful for overriding
inherited terminal styles when composing styled strings.

Contributed by James M Snell in [#​58437](https://redirect.github.com/nodejs/node/pull/58437).

author: ianphilips
body:
The `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` error in Google Cloud Monitoring was due to exceeding the 200,000 active time series limit per monitored resource, caused by unbounded cardinality in custom metric labels.

Changes were made to reduce metric cardinality:

*   In `backend/shared/src/websockets/server.ts`:
    *   A `getTopicCategory` function was added to categorize dynamic websocket `topic` labels (e.g., `answer/ID/update`) into a bounded set of categories (e.g., `answer`, `contract`, `user`).
    *   The `ws/broadcasts_sent` metric now uses a `category` label instead of the raw `topic`.

*   In `backend/api/src/app.ts`:
    *   The `endpoint` label, which contained dynamic IDs, was removed from `http/request_count` and `http/request_latency` metrics.
    *   Only the `baseEndpoint` (normalized path) and `method` labels are retained.

*   In `backend/shared/src/supabase/init.ts`:
    *   The `query` and `endpoint` labels, which contained dynamic SQL queries and full endpoint paths, were removed from `pg/transaction_duration` and `pg/query_count` metrics.
    *   Metrics now use `baseEndpoint` or `job` and `successStr` for bounded cardinality.

These changes ensure that metric labels no longer create an unbounded number of unique time series, preventing future quota exhaustion. Metrics are expected to resume normal operation within 24 hours as old, high-cardinality time series expire.

author: chokobole
body:
This PR implements features required for https://github.com/zk-rabbit/zkx/pull/13.

- Added support for externally configuring parallel execution to enable term-based parallelization.

- Updated the interface to accept dynamically ranked tensors as arguments. Since the number of scalar multiplications cannot be inferred from the tensor shape in this case, a new degree attribute is introduced to explicitly provide this information.

- Based on recent internal benchmarks, we observed a mismatch between window bit sizes computed using theoretical complexity and those that yield optimal performance in practice. To address this, we added support for specifying the window bit size via an attribute.

- **Auto-merge disabled**: Manual testing required for iOS apps before merge
- **Security scanning**: Automated security checks for mobile app vulnerabilities  
- **Release notes**: Automatic generation for App Store releases
- **Branch cleanup**: Automated cleanup of feature branches after merge

## Testing
This implementation is optimized for iOS/Swift projects where manual device testing is critical before code reaches production. Auto-merge is deliberately disabled to ensure:
- Physical device testing on multiple iOS versions
- App Store compliance verification

- Performance testing under real device conditions

author: paulhendricks
body:
## Summary

Updates the `Prompt` enum to use `u32` instead of `u16` for integer-based prompt representations. The change affects both `Prompt::IntegerArray` and `Prompt::ArrayOfIntegerArray` variants, as well as associated `impl_from_for_*` macro implementations.

## Motivation

The original use of `u16` may have been based on the assumption that token ID values would not exceed the vocabulary size of models like GPT-2 or GPT-3 (i.e. 50256 tokens). 

While that assumption held previously, newer models frequently exceed this range. Allowing `u32` values would enable inference libraries to use `u32` token IDs and larger vocabulary sizes without needing to truncate while batching.

I fully recognize this is a breaking change to the public API:
- Users of `Prompt::IntegerArray` or `Prompt::ArrayOfIntegerArray` with `u16` inputs will encounter compile-time errors
- Pattern matches and constructors relying on the `u16` variant types must be updated to use `u32`

However, I think that this is in line with the scope and mission of `async-openai` as the [OpenAI OpenAPI schema does not specify the maximum token ID value](https://github.com/openai/openai-openapi/blob/manual_spec/openapi.yaml#L19946). 

And while users of `Prompt::IntegerArray` or `Prompt::ArrayOfIntegerArray` with `u16` inputs will need to update, conversion of `u16` to `u32` is lossless and won't cause any runtime issues. And the benefits of future proofing and greater compatibility outweigh prioritizing smaller vocabulary sizes from the previous GPT-2/GPT-3 era.

Thank you for your consideration!

author: atian25
body:
A Graphviz visualization page was implemented with interactive node selection and downstream highlighting.

*   **Dependencies**: `@hpcc-js/wasm`, `d3`, `d3-selection`, and `d3-zoom` were added to `package.json` to enable Graphviz rendering and D3.js-based interactive features.
*   **Core Component**: A new `src/components/GraphvizViewer.vue` component was created.
    *   It uses `@hpcc-js/wasm` to render DOT language into an SVG.
    *   `d3.js` is utilized to parse node connections from the rendered SVG, manage original node colors, and implement interactive features.
    *   Clicking a node triggers `highlightDownstream(nodeId)`, which performs a depth-first search via `getDownstreamNodes` to identify all downstream dependencies.
    *   Selected nodes are highlighted in red, downstream nodes in orange, and unrelated elements are dimmed.
    *   `resetHighlight()` restores the original graph appearance.
    *   D3's zoom and pan behavior was added to the SVG, along with a `fitToScreen()` function and click-outside-to-reset functionality.
    *   Multiple sample DOT graphs are included for demonstration.
*   **Application Integration**: `src/App.vue` was updated to display the `GraphvizViewer` component as the main content.
*   **Documentation**: A `GRAPHVIZ_DEMO.md` file was created, detailing the implemented features, technical architecture, and usage instructions.

Since the workflow primarily interacts with repository contents (e.g., checking out code and caching dependencies), the `contents: read` permission is sufficient. This limits the `GITHUB_TOKEN` to read-only access to the repository contents, adhering to the principle of least privilege.

The `permissions` block should be added at the root level of the workflow file, ensuring it applies to all jobs in the workflow. No additional imports or dependencies are required.

author: lightinn
body:
This pull request refactors how translations are handled across multiple pages and components in the application. The changes remove the direct use of translation objects and instead pass the locale to components, which dynamically fetch translations. Additionally, the webhook handling logic for Clerk user events has been significantly refactored to improve modularity and error handling.

### Translation Handling Refactor:

* Removed translation imports and `getTranslations` calls from several pages (`src/app/[locale]/admin/event/page.tsx`, `src/app/[locale]/dashboard/page.tsx`, etc.) and replaced them with locale-based dynamic translation fetching within components. This simplifies the page logic and ensures translations are handled uniformly. ([src/app/[locale]/admin/event/page.tsxL5-L7](diffhunk://#diff-64377ef533465655d9d15b99e90a523d7d5987772f46509e682403c6fdb76192L5-L7), [src/app/[locale]/admin/organizer/create/page.tsxL5-L7](diffhunk://#diff-1b652355130ad8047d1503bb359693a3912c5a5be655ce0999d90d047c7fb531L5-L7), [src/app/[locale]/admin/organizer/page.tsxL5-L7](diffhunk://#diff-72a2c8c375a000a0a042bf6cf496264a908c290c0c812f8605141a86f6d3123fL5-L7), [src/app/[locale]/admin/page.tsxL5-L7](diffhunk://#diff-5c1f2735906943c5ba6dd02878f3515f6e25ef8a8b1601cc1dfee4e8df3682b7L5-L7), [src/app/[locale]/dashboard/DashboardClient.tsxR22-L46](diffhunk://#diff-54a86ff9c0a1c1ab763aec0bd6a609862fa2453274ddc9988651e817262d91e9R22-L46))

* Updated components like `DashboardClient`, `BuyerDashboardClient`, and `SellerDashboardClient` to accept `locale` as a prop instead of pre-fetched translations, enabling dynamic translation fetching inside the components. author: copilot
body:
This PR implements a comprehensive automated release workflow using Google's Release Please to streamline the release process for the SurrealDB Python SDK. The implementation includes multi-environment publishing, automated validation, and complete documentation.

## 🚀 Key Features

### Release Please Integration
- **Automated Release PRs**: Release Please automatically creates release PRs based on conventional commits
- **Semantic Versioning**: Automatic version bumping following semantic versioning rules
- **Changelog Generation**: Automated changelog creation from conventional commit messages
- **Python Package Support**: Configured for Python package management with `pyproject.toml`

### Multi-Environment Publishing Strategy

#### Development Environment (`dev` branch)
```bash
# Triggers on push to dev branch
# Version: 1.0.4.dev123 (with run number suffix)
# Destination: Test PyPI
pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ surrealdb
```

#### Pre-Production Environment (`pre-prod` branch)
```bash
# Triggers on push to pre-prod branch  
# Version: 1.0.4rc1 (release candidate)
# Destination: Test PyPI
pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ surrealdb==1.0.4rc1
```

#### Production Environment (`main` branch)
```bash
# Triggers on Release Please release creation
# Version: 1.0.5 (semantic version)
# Destination: PyPI
pip install surrealdb==1.0.5
```

### Security & Quality Assurance
- **OIDC Trusted Publishing**: No API tokens required, uses GitHub's OIDC for PyPI authentication
- **Pre-Release Validation**: Integrates with existing `tests.yml` and `stability.yml` workflows
- **Post-Release Validation**: Automated verification of package availability and installation
- **Version Consistency**: Ensures version alignment across `pyproject.toml`, `__init__.py`, and manifest

## 📁 Files Added/Modified

### New Workflow Files
- `.github/workflows/release-please.yml` - Main Release Please workflow
- `.github/workflows/build-and-publish.yml` - Multi-environment package building and publishing
- `.github/workflows/validate-release.yml` - Post-release validation and testing

### Configuration Files
- `release-please-config.json` - Release Please configuration for Python packages
- `.release-please-manifest.json` - Version tracking manifest (current: 1.0.4)

### Updated Files
- `src/surrealdb/__init__.py` - Added `__version__` attribute for version tracking
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml` - Added `workflow_call` support for integration
- `.github/workflows/stability.yml` - Added `workflow_call` support for integration
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` - Comprehensive release process documentation

## 📝 Conventional Commits Support

The workflow supports all conventional commit types:

```bash
# Feature (minor version bump)
git commit -m "feat: add connection pooling support"

# Bug fix (patch version bump)
git commit -m "fix: resolve timeout issue in WebSocket connections"

# Breaking change (major version bump)
git commit -m "feat!: remove deprecated authentication methods"

# Documentation, style, refactor, test, chore (no version bump)
git commit -m "docs: update installation guide for Python 3.13"
```

## 🔄 Workflow Integration

The implementation preserves all existing functionality:
- ✅ Existing test matrix (Python 3.9-3.13, SurrealDB 2.1.1-2.1.4)
- ✅ Code stability checks (ruff, black)
- ✅ Package import functionality
- ✅ All existing CI/CD triggers and behaviors

## 🧪 Validation

Comprehensive testing confirms:
- All workflow files are valid YAML with proper GitHub Actions structure
- JSON configuration files are syntactically correct
- Version consistency across all tracking files
- Package import functionality preserved
- Documentation includes all required sections
- Conventional commit examples provided

## 📚 Usage Examples

### For Contributors
```bash
# Development workflow
git checkout dev
git commit -m "feat: add new database operation"
git push origin dev
# → Triggers dev build to Test PyPI

# Release candidate workflow  
git checkout pre-prod
git merge dev
git push origin pre-prod
# → Triggers RC build to Test PyPI

# Production release
git checkout main
git merge pre-prod
git push origin main
# → Release Please creates release PR
# → After merge, triggers production build to PyPI
```

### For Users
```bash
# Install development version
pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ surrealdb

# Install specific release candidate
pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ --extra-index-url https://pypi.org/simple/ surrealdb==1.0.5rc1

# Install stable release
pip install surrealdb==1.0.5
```

This implementation provides 100% automated releases with comprehensive validation, ensuring reliable package delivery while maintaining code quality and security standards.

body:
The `CycleState` was initially introduced as a flexible mechanism for scheduling plugins to share state. Currently the prefix plugin uses this to share the prompt chunk hashes between Scorer and PostCycle extension points.

We have since expanded the plugin framework beyond the scheduler. And we have decided to deprecate the `PostCycle` extension point in favor of the `PreRequest`. Expanding the `CycleState` to the entire request lifecycle allows plugins to share state beyond those extension points defined in scheduler.

I discussed this refactor with @nirrozenbaum in Slack.

Changes:
- Moved `cycle_state.go` to `pkg/epp/plugins/cycle_state.go`
- Added `CycleState` param to `PreRequest`
- Updated references accordingly


This is a PURE REFACTOR. No change of logic.

@kfswain Pls also comment.

## Summary
- Implement complete framework for storing and managing AI-generated poster visual metadata
- Add JSON-based flexible metadata storage with structured accessor methods
- Create extensible service architecture ready for Claude API integration
- Provide rake tasks for batch processing and individual poster analysis

## Features Implemented

### Database Schema
- Added `visual_metadata` JSON column to posters table
- Supports nested structure: visual, thematic, technical, collectibility, market_appeal
- Flexible schema accommodates future metadata additions

### Model Enhancements
- Added metadata accessor methods to Poster model
- Helper methods for common queries (art_style, color_palette, mood, themes, etc.)
- Validates metadata presence and structure

### Analysis Service
- `PosterMetadataService` with extensible analysis framework
- Sample metadata structure demonstrates expected format
- Ready for Claude API integration (TODO: actual API calls)
- Batch processing support for multiple posters

### Rake Tasks
- `posters:analyze[id]` - Analyze specific poster by ID
- `posters:analyze_all` - Batch analyze all posters with images
- `posters:show_metadata[id]` - Display stored metadata in pretty JSON
- `posters:stats` - Show analysis coverage and common art styles

## Test Plan
- [x] Database migration applied successfully
- [x] Model accessor methods tested with sample metadata
- [x] Service analysis framework tested with mock data
- [x] Rake tasks functional with current poster data (772 posters with images)
- [x] Factory trait for posters with images
- [x] Comprehensive test coverage (345 examples, 0 failures)
- [x] Clean linting (0 offenses) and security scan (0 warnings)

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Analyze a specific poster
rake "posters:analyze[1076]"

# Show stored metadata  
rake "posters:show_metadata[1076]"

# Check analysis statistics
rake posters:stats
```

```ruby
# Access metadata in Ruby
poster = Poster.find(1076)
poster.has_metadata? # => true
poster.metadata_art_style # => "minimalist"
poster.metadata_color_palette # => ["black", "white", "blue"] 
poster.metadata_mood # => ["peaceful", "dreamy"]
```

## Future Enhancement Ready
This framework enables powerful features like:
- Visual similarity recommendations ("Find posters like this one")
- Color scheme matching for room decoration
- Mood-based browsing ("Show me calming artwork")
- Art style categorization and filtering

author: ignaciosica
body:
Is there any particular reason we use the original ast for `ProgramSpec`?

I came across this while refactoring some calls to `linearize` in the tests. I realized that if we use the original ast for the `ProgramSpec` and apply some opts through the new `opts_to_apply` api, the original ast won't correctly track the `applied_opts`. If we want the state to live in the uops, we need to use `modified_ast` for `ProgramSpec`.

Notice that in order to print the `applied_opts`, `modified_ast` is used in line 39.

https://github.com/tinygrad/tinygrad/blob/9d995c2a4d7725add3412c5411de2d6bfdafff01/tinygrad/engine/realize.py#L17-L48

I'm asking this question and not considering this bug because the original ast was also used for ProgramSpec before all the refactors that have been taking place lately, so maybe there is a reason behind it.

Currently, Codespaces may open with JetBrains Gateway by default for some users, which can lead to an inconsistent development experience across the team. This configuration standardizes the experience by ensuring VS Code Web is always the default editor when launching Codespaces.

This pull request introduces significant changes to enhance student management functionality across the application. The updates include injecting and utilizing `StudentService`, creating new pages for managing and editing student data, and improving existing workflows to support asynchronous operations. Below are the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Dependency Injection and Service Integration
* Added `StudentService` as a dependency in `AdminMainWindow`, `LoginWindow`, and `ParentHealthDeclarationPage` to enable student-related operations. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6d5f1327ab5d54f299d61117bec8cb37d04e1755f2c6ab4d9abf5166d463b06bL11-R26)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4ff6350f9c645176cc1dd212fa9a5c9d02b2d120adae5c552710489fcbbd7e00R16-R24)`)
* Updated constructors to inject `StudentService` and pass it to relevant pages, such as `StudentManagementPage` and `AdminMainWindow`. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6d5f1327ab5d54f299d61117bec8cb37d04e1755f2c6ab4d9abf5166d463b06bL11-R26)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4ff6350f9c645176cc1dd212fa9a5c9d02b2d120adae5c552710489fcbbd7e00L49-R51)`)

### Student Management Features
* Created `CreateUpdateStudent.xaml` and `CreateUpdateStudent.xaml.cs` for adding and editing student information. This includes UI elements for student details and methods for saving or updating student data. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-93fe27437e8f0439e18adef59e857dc3ba876cffbeb260e48dfd1f09cf2c7d30R1-R102)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ddb73cab24546ece8a4afcbcf62352de44493f4288056b8259327ba77ed5b33bR1-R71)`)
* Enhanced `StudentManagementPage.xaml` and `StudentManagementPage.xaml.cs` with new UI designs, filtering functionality, and CRUD operations for managing students. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-697350585063c424ea383aaf8f147922766790759aee3bbcc7fd9ac2e8b7cf16L4-R91)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2058b5231fbc9595614d45cb778cbeed55dfc540989acd2d0d690017ab930c93L1-R94)`)

### Asynchronous Operations
* Refactored methods in `ParentHealthDeclarationPage.xaml.cs` and `MedicalRegistrationFormWindow.xaml.cs` to use asynchronous calls for fetching student data. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f2c8ab82bca71109201a014338dee837551eb7064adaf8938ba021a7bf3a55f7L48-R52)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a6bb344f0a358aca510de5ca046d8f255a4d8cf2cdb999fbe55f395e683610e3L27-R27)`, `[[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a6bb344f0a358aca510de5ca046d8f255a4d8cf2cdb999fbe55f395e683610e3L37-R37)`)

These changes collectively improve the application's ability to manage student data efficiently, provide a better user experience, and ensure scalability for future enhancements.

author: umruumum
body:
## Summary
ポップアップUIのレイアウト改善と、新機能「ドメイングループ名設定」を追加しました。

## 🎨 ポップアップレイアウト改善

### レイアウト全体の最適化
- ポップアップ幅を300px→320pxに拡張してより多くのスペースを確保
- paddingを調整してバランスの良いレイアウトを実現

### UI要素のはみ出し問題を修正
- **グループ色選択ダイアログ**: 幅を280px→260pxに調整して枠内に収束
- **ドメイン色設定**: color-selectの最大幅制限とflex-wrapで柔軟なレイアウト
- **除外ドメイン設定**: 入力フィールドとボタンを7:3比率に調整
- 専用CSSクラス（domain-add）で他のボタンに影響しないよう分離

## 🏷️ ドメイングループ名設定機能（新機能）

### 機能概要
- ドメインごとにカスタムグループ名を設定可能
- 除外ドメイン・色設定と同様の直感的なUI
- 既存グループのタイトルをリアルタイム更新

### UI特徴
- **緑色ベースのカラーテーマ**で他セクションと視覚的に区別
- **2つの入力フィールド**: ドメイン名とカスタムグループ名
- **現在のタブ設定機能**: ワンクリックで現在のタブのドメインに名前設定
- **設定一覧と削除**: 設定済みドメイン名の確認と個別削除

### 技術実装
- **ストレージ管理**: `domainNames`オブジェクトでChrome storage管理
- **優先順位**: カスタム名 > ドメイン名の順でタイトル決定
- **ESModule対応**: 動的インポートとフォールバック機能で安定性向上

## 🐛 修正された問題

### サービスワーカー安定化
- ESModuleインポートエラーによるサービスワーカー停止を修正
- バックグラウンドスクリプトとの通信エラーを解決
- 初期化チェックとフォールバック機能を追加

### レイアウト問題
- 各種UI要素がポップアップ枠からはみ出る問題を解決
- ボタンサイズとレイアウトの最適化
- レスポンシブ対応の向上

## 📚 ドキュメント更新

### README.md改善
- **インストール方法**: Releaseページからのダウンロードを推奨方法に変更
- **機能一覧**: ファビコン色抽出、カスタムグループ名等の最新機能を追加
- **今後の予定**: 実装済み機能の進捗を正確に反映

## Test plan
- [x] ポップアップの全要素が枠内に正しく表示される
- [x] グループ色選択ダイアログが正常に動作する
- [x] ドメイングループ名設定が正常に動作する
- [x] 現在のタブのドメイン名設定機能が動作する
- [x] 設定一覧の表示と削除機能が正常に動作する
- [x] 除外ドメイン入力が7:3比率で表示される
- [x] 他のボタンサイズに影響しない
- [x] サービスワーカーが安定して動作する
- [x] 既存グループのタイトルがリアルタイム更新される

- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code documentation](http://docs.anthropic.com/s/claude-code-github-actions).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: copilot
body:
This PR resolves the Railway deployment health check failures caused by Prisma schema path resolution issues during container startup.

## Issue Summary
Railway deployments were failing with repeated errors:
```
Error: Could not load --schema from provided path prisma/schema.prisma: file or directory not found
```

This caused the health check at `/api/ping` to fail, leading to continuous container restarts.

## Root Cause
The issue was caused by:
1. **Explicit schema path flags** causing path resolution conflicts in Railway's deployment environment
2. **Prisma client generation during deployment** instead of build phase, causing startup delays
3. **Inconsistent working directory context** between build and deploy phases

## Solution
### 1. Use Prisma Auto-Detection
Removed explicit `--schema=prisma/schema.prisma` flags from all Prisma commands, allowing Prisma to use its default auto-detection behavior:

```toml
# Before
npx prisma generate --schema=./prisma/schema.prisma

# After  
npx prisma generate
```

### 2. Move Prisma Client Generation to Build Phase
Updated both `railway.toml` and `nixpacks.toml` to generate the Prisma client during the build phase instead of deployment:

```toml
[build]
buildCommand = "... && npx prisma generate && ..."

[deploy]
startCommand = "npx prisma migrate deploy && node index.js"
```

### 3. Enhanced Debugging and Error Handling
Added comprehensive debugging output and graceful error handling:
- File structure verification during build and deploy
- Prisma client generation verification
- Graceful migration failure handling to prevent startup blocking

### 4. Updated Documentation
Enhanced `RAILWAY.md` with improved troubleshooting guidance and deployment process documentation.

## Benefits
- ✅ **Faster deployments**: Prisma client generated once during build, not on every deployment
- ✅ **More reliable**: Eliminates path resolution issues using Prisma's standard behavior
- ✅ **Better error handling**: Graceful handling of migration failures prevents infinite restart loops
- ✅ **Improved debugging**: Comprehensive output for future troubleshooting
- ✅ **Standard workflow**: Aligns with Prisma best practices and Railway deployment patterns

## Testing
The changes include extensive debugging output that will help verify the fix works correctly in the Railway environment. The deployment should now:
1. Successfully generate Prisma client during build
2. Apply migrations during startup (with graceful failure handling)
3. Start the Node.js server successfully
4. Respond to health checks at `/api/ping`

Fixes #62.

This pull request introduces Firebase integration into the Balanced Meal app, enabling backend services like Firestore and Firebase initialization. Additionally, it includes updates to translations, app themes, routing, and the data layer for handling food-related entities. Below is a breakdown of the most important changes grouped by theme:

### Firebase Integration
* Added Firebase dependencies in `android/app/build.gradle.kts` and `android/settings.gradle.kts` for Firebase services. (`[[1]](diffhunk://#diff-852897104c5cf350a945bb63cd9836c04ab5209a74900a1e8938092f6b9d68fbR3-R5)`, `[[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b846529d3b9af5e34dfb0174742f9dc3d52bcd97761555bc61271a7a868870b9R22-R24)`)
* Added `google-services.json` for Firebase project configuration. (`[android/app/google-services.jsonR1-R29](diffhunk://#diff-6e90a675296b4fc8873eba10f2a741ea4f511bf93b7244a005e97bbb97e27b97R1-R29)`)
* Created `firebase.json` to define Firebase options for the app. (`[firebase.jsonR1](diffhunk://#diff-3f7c92e2669f851959cda8776100cf4e921faefe7dff0061c0e21f7d2ac65122R1)`)

### Data Layer Enhancements
* Introduced `OrderRemoteDataSource` and its implementation to fetch food data (vegetables, carbs, meats) from Firestore. author: acavelan
body:
## Distribution "truncate" parameter

This adds a truncation parameter to the samplers. 

Anytime we can specify a distribution, we can also specify an optional **truncate** parameter, which will cap the distirbution samples to the chosen maximum value.

For example, here we cap gamma samples with CV 2 to 25.0 in order to avoid having hosts with unrealistically high availability:
```XML
<mosq minInfectedThreshold="0.001">
                    <mosqRestDuration value="3"/>
                    <extrinsicIncubationPeriod value="11"/>
                    <mosqLaidEggsSameDayProportion value="0.313"/>
                    <mosqSeekingDuration value="0.33"/>
                    <mosqSurvivalFeedingCycleProbability value="0.623"/>
                    <availability distr="gamma" CV="2" truncate="25.0"/>
                    <mosqProbBiting mean="0.95" variance="0"/>
                    <mosqProbFindRestSite mean="0.95" variance="0"/>
                    <mosqProbResting mean="0.99" variance="0"/>
                    <mosqProbOvipositing value="0.88"/>
                    <mosqHumanBloodIndex value="0.939"/>
</mosq>
```

- Fix crash issue caused by translator instance being deleted while qApp still using it
- Add .cache and .cursor to .gitignore ignore list

Problem:
When plugins are stopped, the translator instance is deleted with its parent object,
but qApp is still using the instance, causing a crash.

Solution:
- Optimize translator instance lifecycle management
- Ensure translator instance is released after qApp stops using it

Task: https://pms.uniontech.com/task-view-378321.html

## Summary by Sourcery

Prevent crashes when stopping plugins by re-parenting the translator instance to qApp and update .gitignore

Bug Fixes:
- Re-parent QTranslator to qApp to ensure it remains alive while qApp uses it, avoiding deletion-related crashes

Chores:
- Add .cache and .cursor entries to .gitignore

author: shihong5858
body:
Windows conversion errors and missing logs were addressed.

*   In `components/resource_manager.py`, the hardcoded PATH separator was replaced with `os.pathsep` to ensure cross-platform compatibility, resolving issues with binary tool discovery (e.g., 7z) on Windows.
*   `components/conversion/converter.py` was updated to automatically generate a detailed error log on the user's desktop upon conversion failure, even when debug mode is disabled.
    *   This log, named `eReader_CBZ_Error_[timestamp].txt`, captures conversion steps, error messages, and environment details, including the PATH.
    *   Windows desktop path resolution was made more robust using `USERPROFILE` and fallback mechanisms.
    *   The `_create_cbz` method now passes conversion log data for comprehensive error reporting.
*   Enhanced 7z tool path handling within `converter.py` includes more detailed logging of its availability and setup process.

```js
const foo /* #__PURE__ */ = pureOperation(); // INVALID: "=" not allowed after annotation
```
[Reference to the spec](https://github.com/javascript-compiler-hints/compiler-notations-spec/blob/main/pure-notation-spec.md#1-directly-preceding-a-call)

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
With PR [cert-management#512](https://github.com/gardener/cert-management/pull/512) the `Issuer` resources must have the `cert.gardener.cloud/class` as specified in the deployment of the cert-controller-manager. Formerly it was only required for `Certificate` resources. It was introduced to avoid races if two instances of the cert-controller-manager use the same namespace for its issuer and only reconcile their own issuers.

**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:
Fixes #

Change will only be effective with the next release of the cert-management.

## Description **TLDR:** Adds support for executing page unload actions during navigation in deployed mode, refactors related components, and improves action handling. Problem Page unload actions were not triggered during navigation in deployed mode, leading to incomplete workflows especially for cleanup. Root cause The application lacked integration for executing unload actions on page transitions, and related components did not properly handle navigation or action execution. Solution This PR handles the integration of page unload action execution during navigation in deployed mode. It introduces selectors for unload actions, refactors the MenuItem component for better navigation handling, and improves the PluginActionSaga for executing plugin actions. author: trodicode
body:
This commit introduces a new, simplified internationalization (i18n) system focusing only on static text within HTML files. It replaces the previous i18next-based implementation (V4.0.0-V4.0.4) which has been reverted in the initial part of this commit sequence.

Key Changes:

1.  **Revert of Previous i18n (V4.0.0-V4.0.4):**
    *   Removed i18next library, `js/i18n.js`, `locales/` directory.
    *   Removed all associated `data-i18n` tags from HTML.
    *   Reverted `js/admin.js`, `js/main.js`, `js/login.js` to use hardcoded English for dynamic messages; API data is displayed as-is.
    *   Set functional baseline to V0.3.1 before these new changes.

2.  **New Simplified i18n System:**
    *   Created `js/i18n-static.js`:
        *   Contains an embedded JavaScript object with 'en' and 'fr' translations.
        *   Manages language selection (via global `setLanguage` function) and persistence in `localStorage`.
        *   Translates elements with `data-i18n-static` (for textContent) and `data-i18n-static-placeholder` (for placeholder attributes).
        *   Translates `document.title` using `data-i18n-page-title-static` on the `<html>` tag.
    *   Updated `index.html`, `login.html`, and `admin.html`:
        *   Added `<script src="js/i18n-static.js"></script>`.
        *   Added language switcher buttons (EN/FR).
        *   Tagged all static HTML text elements (labels, buttons, titles, headings, select options, help text, etc.) with `data-i18n-static` or `data-i18n-static-placeholder`.
        *   Original English text is retained in HTML as fallback.
    *   Populated `js/i18n-static.js` with comprehensive EN/FR translations for all tagged static content.

3.  **Scope:**
    *   This i18n system translates only static text found directly in HTML.
    *   Data from API calls (e.g., ticket statuses, urgencies) is displayed as-is (in its original language from Airtable).
    *   JavaScript-generated messages (e.g., validation errors, success alerts) remain in their hardcoded default language (English).

4.  **Versioning:**
    *   Updated the application version in `admin.html` to `V0.5.0`.

## Summary

Transforms the basic "Parking Lot" issue (#11) into a comprehensive support system for GitHub training participants by adding structured documentation, templates, and resources.

## Problem

Issue #11 had minimal guidance ("Post any questions you may have here during the training") which didn't provide structure or help participants ask effective questions during the GitHub for Developers training.

## Solution

### 📚 New Documentation Files

**`docs/parking-lot-guide.md`** - Complete 4.9KB guide covering:
- Step-by-step instructions for using the Parking Lot
- Question categories (Git Workflow, GitHub Features, Activity Help, Technical Issues, Best Practices)
- Structured templates for different question types
- Community guidelines and escalation paths
- Quick reference links to training resources

**`docs/question-templates.md`** - Ready-to-use templates for:
- Git workflow questions with command examples
- GitHub features questions
- Activity-specific help requests
- Technical troubleshooting
- Best practices inquiries

**`docs/faq.md`** - Comprehensive FAQ (5.0KB) addressing:
- Git vs GitHub fundamentals
- Branching, merging, and Pull Request workflows
- Merge conflict resolution strategies
- Common troubleshooting scenarios
- Learning resources and next steps

**`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/parking-lot-comment-template.md`** - GitHub-optimized comment templates for Issue #11

### 🔗 Enhanced Integration

- **README.md**: Added prominent Parking Lot guide link in Class Resources section
- **Training Documentation**: Added Parking Lot references to all daily materials (`day1.md` through `day4.md`)

### 🧪 Validation

Created and ran comprehensive test script validating:
- All files exist and contain proper content
- Cross-references and links work correctly  
- Integration with existing training materials

## Benefits

Training participants now have:
- ✅ Clear guidance on asking effective questions
- ✅ Professional templates improving question quality
- ✅ Comprehensive FAQ covering common Git/GitHub issues
- ✅ Easy access from all training materials
- ✅ Structured support system instead of basic issue

## Example Usage

Before:
```markdown
"Git isn't working"
```

After (using templates):
```markdown
### 🅿️ Git Workflow Question

**Question:** Getting "Permission denied" when trying to push

**Context:** Trying to push my first commit for Activity 1

**Command I used:**
```bash
git push origin add-caption-myname

**Error message:**
```
remote: Permission to devtrainNIC/Initial-repo.git denied to myusername.
fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/devtrainNIC/Initial-repo.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403
```

**Resources I've checked:** GitHub docs on authentication
**Urgency:** High - blocking my progress
```

Fixes #11.

body:
## Description

<!-- Briefly describe the changes you've made and link any relevant issues (e.g., "Fixes #123"). -->
<!-- If the PR includes UI changes, please attach a screenshot or GIF to illustrate the modifications. -->
This PR fixes https://github.com/dust-tt/tasks/issues/3286.

We have some stuck workflows in WorkOS were we fail to add the verified domain in our DB because we have a unique constraint that WorkOS does not have. On WorkOS side, domain can be associated with multiple organizations, but can only be administrated by one. There is no way to tell from the API which organization owns it.

This PR changes the logic of the WorkOS webhooks for the following:
- on `domain_verified` (trigger when proper DNS record verification has been completed)
  - if the domain is not associated with any other organization, then we upsert it
  - if the domain is associated with another organization in the **same region**, we delete it from the DB and WorkOS
  - if the domain is associated with another organisation in **another region**, we throw an error that requires engineering action 
- on `organization_updated`
  - if the domain does not exist in our DB and is not associated with another organization, we proceed and save it in our DB
  - otherwise we silently swallow the errors and log

## Summary
OpenAPI v1仕様に対応した漫画グラフ可視化フロントエンドアプリケーションを実装しました。

### 主な機能
- **漫画作品検索**: 作品名による検索とインタラクティブなグラフ可視化

## Description

When using the CopyObject API, S3 has the ability to calculate a server-side checksum. In the docs they write:

When copying objects, you can choose to use a different checksum algorithm for the object. Whether you choose to use the same algorithm or a new one, Amazon S3 calculates a new checksum value after the object is copied. Amazon S3 doesn't directly copy the value of the checksum.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/copy-object.html

With a copy command, the checksum of the object is a direct checksum of the full object. If the object was originally uploaded using a multipart upload, the checksum value changes even though the data doesn't.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/checking-object-integrity.html

For example if you upload a multi-part object, then CopyObject on it, the copy will become a full-object checksum, no longer the composite one. But the caller of the CopyObject API does not need to provide that full-object checksum, it is instead computed server-side.

This PR introduces this functionality and fixes a bug where we were seeing a log entry "sio: authentication failed" for decryptPartChecksums in certain scenarios

## Motivation and Context

Fixes a bug in the CopyObject API and adds missing functionality.

## How to test this PR?

Using the mint tests in minio-go.

## Types of changes
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Optimization (provides speedup with no functional changes)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)

author: vaalyn
body:
**Fixes issue:**
x

**Proposed changes:**

Due to wrongly mapped `aac` mime type in the upstream library `league/mime-type-detection` which mapps `aac` to `audio/acc` instead of `audio/aac` we encounter the following error when trying to save an .aac file via the UI after editing some metadata:
> PHP Fatal error:  Uncaught RuntimeException: Cannot write tag formats based on file type.

I have already submitted a PR to the upstream repo of the library but until this is acutally merged we can fix this by adjusting the `lookupMimeType` method in our `MimeTypeExtensionMap` to first look into our `ADDED_MIME_TYPES` constant and providing our own mapping through that.

body:
### Added

- Serverless tracker functions may now accept shapes other than rectangles (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9517>)

- \[CLI\] A more helpful error message is now raised if a loaded auto-annotation function has no `spec` attribute (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9530>)

- `CVAT_CACHE_ITEM_MAX_SIZE` option that limits size of data chunk at CVAT level. Generating data that exceeds the size will result in an exception. (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9524>)

- CVAT server tracks `last_activity_date` of a user, the field is updated once a day (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9554>)

- Filtration by username to Grafana dashboards (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9555>)

### Changed

- Updated zooming algorithm, it works much smoother with touchpads and a little bit smoother for mice (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9523>)

- Kvrocks: configured auto compaction at scheduled time. (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9524>)

- Nuclio tracker functions are no longer passed the previous frame's shapes when continuing the tracking (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9548>)

- Endpoints accepting annotations as input now check that shapes have point and element counts that are appropriate for the shape type (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9556>)

### Fixed

- Reduced excessive DB use in dataset export (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9472>)

- Page size selector on organization page was not working (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9521>)

- Incorrect width of project field on webhook setup page (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/XXXX>)

- Relevant task quality reports now can be reused in project quality reports (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9538>)

- Fixing 3d export for projects (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/pull/9540>)

### Security

- Added missing file name validation when initiating an import process from a file uploaded via the TUS protocol (<https://github.com/cvat-ai/cvat/security/advisories/GHSA-frpr-5w6q-hh4f>)

author: jimmychongz

Calling sock_release() directly when worker thread creation fails may leave the socket not properly
shut down, potentially causing incomplete resource cleanup. This change adds a call to kernel_sock_shutdown() before releasing the socket, ensuring the connection is properly closed and reducing the risk of resource leaks or abnormal network states.

#### Description

Move handling of `Json` from `R2dbcResult` to `PrimitiveTypeMapper`.

A small problem with usage of Type mappers is that reading of values doesn't go through type mappers by default, and all the column types that want to use it should override `readObject` and call `rs.getObject(index, <KotlinType>::class.java, this)` to make it working.

For example, if we read `boolean` from Json (using `BooleanColumnType`) that column type must override `readObject`, otherwise it will receive `Json` object instead of "boolean string"

---

#### Type of Change

Affected databases:
- [X] Postgres

author: weinohgodwin
body:
### Pull Request Description

---

### **Title:**

Add Core Features for Decentralized Video Platform: Creator Onboarding, Uploads, Purchases, and Premium Subscriptions

---

### **Overview:**

This pull request implements the foundational logic for a decentralized video streaming platform, enabling content creators to monetize uploads, users to purchase and stream content, and subscribers to access premium features. Administrative controls for platform governance are also included.

---

### **Key Features Implemented:**

---

#### 👑 **Admin Functions**

* `toggle-contract-pause`: Allows platform administrators to pause/unpause all user and creator activities.
* `add-administrator`: Grants new principals administrative privileges, excluding the burn address.

---

#### 🎬 **Creator Workflow**

* `register-as-creator`: Allows a user to become a registered content creator.
* `upload-video`: Enables creators to upload a video with metadata:

  * Validates that contract is not paused.
  * Requires a non-empty title, description, and a valid content hash.
  * Stores video info, initializes views and revenue.

---

#### 🧑‍💻 **User Interactions**

* `purchase-video`:

  * Allows users to pay the listed `price` to access a video.
  * Revenue is transferred to the creator immediately.
  * Views and revenue are incremented atomically.
* `subscribe-premium`:

  * Grants time-bound premium access.
  * Each unit of `duration` costs `10 STX` and equates to 144 blocks (\~1 day).
  * Subscription is stored with an expiry block height.

---

#### 🔍 **Read-only Utilities**

* `get-video-details`: Returns full video metadata.
* `get-creator-revenue`: Fetches a creator’s cumulative revenue (fallbacks to `0`).
* `is-premium-subscriber`: Returns `true` if user’s subscription has not expired.

---

#### 🔒 **State Controls**

* Pausing the contract disables uploads, purchases, and subscriptions.
* Contract starts with the deploying address (`contract-owner`) as the sole admin.

---

### **Data Flow Summary**

* `videos`: Stores per-video metadata including price, views, and revenue.
* `premium-subscribers`: Tracks users' premium subscription expiry.
* `content-creators`: Principal whitelist for who can upload.
* `administrators`: Controls who can pause/unpause or manage the platform.
* `creator-revenue`: Tracks total earnings for each creator (used via read-only getter).
* `platform-revenue`: Reserved for tracking platform-level income in future versions.

---

author: lucasbordeau
body:
# What this PR does

This PR introduces what’s needed to progressively refactor the useDropdown hooks we have.

It removes useDropdownV2 and renames useDropdown used for multi-page dropdowns to useDropdownContextStateManagement

## The 3 useDropdown hooks

There are currently 3 useDropdown hooks : 

One is used for managing states in some dropdowns that have multiple inner pages with contexts and without recoil. It is limited and would need a separate refactoring, thus I just renamed it.

Then we have useDropdown and useDropdownV2, which followed our multiple versions of recoil state management wrappers.

Now that the state management has been stabilized, we can merge everything on the last version.

## What this refactor will allow next

This refactor will allow to refactor the legacy recoil state management, because useDropdown is depending on legacy recoil states with scopeId. 

Because there are only a dozen of those legacy states left, and the dropdown’s ones are the harder to refactor, because swapping them as-is causes a big QA, and if we have a big QA to do on all dropdowns, better refactor the whole dropdown management and have everything clean.

After this refactor, we will be able to delete the legacy dropdown states, and proceed with the other legacy states, then removing all the legacy recoil state mangament.

## How do we allow progressive refactoring ?

There are many places where useDropdown is used.

To have an easier refactoring process, we want to merge multiple small pull requests so that it is easier to QA and review.

For this we will maintain both legacy component state and component state V2 in parallel for isDropdownOpen, so that the new hooks `useOpenDropdown` , `useCloseDropdown` are doing the same thing than `useDropdown` and `useDropdownV2` . 

Thus for the moment, whether we use the legacy hooks or the new ones, the effects are the same. 

And we can have dropdowns operating on the old states and the new states living side by side in the app.

## Flakiness

If I had to re-run tests in the CI due to flakiness, I add the incident [on Notion][2]

## Checklist

I have:

- [ ] Made sure my feature is working on web.
- [ ] Made sure my feature is working on mobile (depending on relevance : real or virtual devices)
- [ ] Written **unit tests** native (and web when implementation is different) for my feature.
- [ ] Added a **screenshot** for UI tickets or deleted the screenshot section if no UI change
- [ ] If my PR is a bugfix, I add the link of the "résolution de problème sur le bug" [on Notion][1]
- [ ] I am aware of all the best practices and respected them.

## Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5f22dd2-45fd-4ec5-8d98-3cd2d95fb78d)

[1]: https://www.notion.so/passcultureapp/R-solution-de-probl-mes-sur-les-bugs-5dd6df8f6a754e6887066cf613467d0a
[2]: https://www.notion.so/passcultureapp/cb45383351b44723a6f2d9e1481ad6bb?v=10fe47258701423985aa7d25bb04cfee&pvs=4

## Best Practices

<details>
  <summary>Click to expand</summary>

These rules apply to files that you make changes to.
If you can't respect one of these rules, be sure to explain why with a comment.
If you consider correcting the issue is too time consuming/complex: create a ticket. Link the ticket in the code.

- In the production code: remove type assertions with `as` (type assertions are removed at compile-time, there is no runtime checking associated with a type assertion. There won’t be an exception or `null` generated if the type assertion is wrong). In certain cases `as const` is acceptable (for example when defining readonly arrays/objects). Using `as` in tests is tolerable.
- Remove bypass type checking with `any` (when you want to accept anything because you will be blindly passing it through without interacting with it, you can use `unknown`). Using `any` in tests is tolerable.
- Remove non-null assertion operators (just like other type assertions, this doesn’t change the runtime behavior of your code, so it’s important to only use `!` when you know that the value can’t be `null` or `undefined`).
- Remove all `@ts-expect-error` and `@eslint-disable`.
- Remove all warnings, and errors that we are used to ignore (`yarn test:lint`, `yarn test:types`, `yarn start:web`...).
- Use `gap` (`ViewGap`) instead of `<Spacer.Column />`, `<Spacer.Row />` or `<Spacer.Flex />`.
- Don't add new "alias hooks" (hooks created to group other hooks together). When adding new logic, this hook will progressively become more complex and harder to maintain.
- Remove logic from components that should be dumb.
- undefined != null : undefined should be used for optionals and null when no value

### Request specific:

- A request must use `react-query`
- A hook that use `react-query` must:
  - folder
    - when used in one feature
      - be in `src/<feature>/queries/`
    - when used by several features
      - be in `src/queries/<the main feature related to the query>/`
  - file
    - when use `useQuery` or hook related (like `useInfiniteQuery`)
      - named `use<the content retrieved by the query>Query.ts`
      - returns the type `UseQueryResult<the content retrieved by the query>`
    - when use `useMutation`
      - named `use<the content mutated by the query>Mutation.ts`
      - returns the type `UseMutationResult<the content mutated by the query>`

### Test specific:

- Avoid mocking internal parts of our code. Ideally, mock only external calls.
- When you see a local variable that is over-written in every test, mock it.
- Prefer `user` to `fireEvent`.
- When mocking feature flags, use `setFeatureFlags`. If not possible, mention which one(s) you want to mock in a comment (example: `jest.spyOn(useFeatureFlagAPI, 'useFeatureFlag').mockReturnValue(true) // WIP_NEW_OFFER_TILE in renderPassPlaylist.tsx` )
- In component tests, replace `await act(async () => {})` and `await waitFor(/* ... */)` by `await screen.findBySomething()`.
- In hooks tests, use `act` by default and `waitFor` as a last resort.
- Make a snapshot test for pages and modals ONLY.
- Make a web specific snapshot when your web page/modal is specific to the web.
- Make an a11y test for web pages.

### Advice:

- Use TDD
- Use Storybook
- Use pair programming/mobs

</details>

author: thorstendb-arm
body:
While adding "gdbtarget" to the extension "RTOS Viewer" I was wondering about the relatively complex handling of variable evaluation inside function handleVariableRequestObject() in src/gdb/GDBDebugSessionBase.ts. The issue was, that some of the RTOS variables could not be evaluated because of the array handling. Struct members were encapsulated into [] brackets where they shouldn't.

I refactored parts of that module to use gdb mi commands, see: https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/GDB_002fMI-Variable-Objects.html
-var-info-expression (for display elements)
-var-info-path-expression (to create and store expressions)

A "major" change is, that array elements are now displayed as "0 = ..." instaed of "[0] = ...".

After this change, the RTOS Viewer displayed FreeRTOS, and my tests with global nested struct / array variables did not show any issue.

body:
Created by `brew bump` --- Created with `brew bump-formula-pr`.
release notes 
## v0.18.11 - 2025-06-25

### 🔥 Breaking Changes
- Remove `namespace` argument from `CacheVolume` by @sipsma in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10586 \
  This arg was only ever meant for internal usage within the API's
  implementation, but previously couldn't be hidden from the public API. Now it
  is properly internal-only and thus not accessible to external clients. Any use
  of the arg should just be removed.
- Changed incorrect `sweep` engine option name to `sweepSize` by @jedevc in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10560
  This option was previously incorrectly named - the docs were correct, but the
  code was not properly updated.

### Added
- New top-level `cloud` API for getting information about the dagger cloud session by @marcosnils in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10580 \
  This includes the `cloud.traceURL` field for getting the current trace URL.
- Allow `--no-mod`/`-M` flag in more places to disable automatic module loading by @jedevc in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10595
- Propagate exit codes properly in shell by @helderco in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10438 \
  The `.exit` builtin was added.

  The `.wait` builtin now accepts a list of job ids to wait for. For example:

  ```sh
  container | from alpine | with-exec false | stdout &
  job1=$!
  container | from alpine | with-exec echo ok | stdout &
  job2=$!
  .echo ".wait $job1 $job2"
  .wait $job1 $job2
  ```

  The above example should exit with status code 1 because `.wait` returns
  the exit of the first command that failed. This is different from Bash
  which returns the exit status of the last command in the list, even if
  it succeeded when others have failed.
- Add `httpAuthUsername` parameter to `git` to allow basic auth with usernames by @grouville in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10605 \
  Additionally this field is populated from the client's git credential helper,
  similarly to passwords.
- You can now set `$DAGGER_PROGRESS` to configure your preferred progress format globally, instead of passing the `--progress` flag every time by @vito in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10617
- Added a new `dots` progress format, which is a much quieter alternative to `plain` suitable for use in CI by @vito in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10617
  This format focuses on printing logs and reduces everything else to just
  green dots and red Xes for success/failure, similar to test runners like RSpec.
  [Demo](https://asciinema.org/a/723921)

### Changed
- shell: use main object description as the fallback in `.help ` by @helderco in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10487
- When a service fails to start, the API will now return a proper `ExecError` so you can see the stdout/stderr and exit code programmatically by @vito in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10585

### Fixed
- Fixed high engine memory usage exacerbated by high log volume and composing multiple modules by @vito in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10578 \
  In one scenario this reduced heap usage from 14GB to 7GB.
- Schema introspection is now cached, as long as the schema doesn't change by @vito in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10579 \
  In the same scenario as the high log volume fix, this further reduced heap usage from 7GB to 1.4GB.
- shell: fixed arguments with pipelines to interpreter builtins not being resolved by @helderco in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10635
- Fixed the `plain` progress format being way more verbose than intended by @vito in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10636
- Fixed `Directory.withSymlink` accidentally escaping from the selected sub-directory by @alexcb in https://github.com/dagger/dagger/pull/10563

### What to do next?
- Read the [documentation](https://docs.dagger.io)
- Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/dagger-io)
- Follow us on [Twitter](https://twitter.com/dagger_io)

View the full release notes at https://github.com/dagger/dagger/releases/tag/v0.18.11.

author: peterbell10
body:
This adds a new API for warming up kernels in parallel:
```python
with (
    ThreadPoolExecutor(2) as pool,
    triton.AsyncCompileMode(pool)
):
    kernel1.warmup(...)
    kernel2.warmup(...)
```

The semantics are that `warmup` launches the compile function in a thread pool and returns a `FutureKernel` object. You can then call `.result()` on the `FutureKernel` to block and wait until the compilation is completed.

Once the `with` region ends we block and wait for all compilation jobs to complete.

You can also choose to run kernels inside the region and in this case the compilation still happens in the thread pool, and the main thread will block waiting for the compilation to finish.

Y offsets get swapped with X offsets when laying down. That results in offsets getting stacked together if you shift vertically while standing, then unshift when resting, eventually going visually off-screen.

author: toshi0806
body:
## Summary

- 新しいElixir実装によりecosystem-managerのパフォーマンスを大幅改善
- 並列処理により12秒→1.5秒の劇的な性能向上を実現
- 全ての品質チェック（テスト・Credo・Dialyzer・フォーマット）をクリア

## Performance Improvements

| モード | 元のBash版 | 新しいElixir版 | 改善率 |
|--------|------------|----------------|--------|
| フルモード | 12+ seconds | ~1.5 seconds | 88% faster |
| 高速モード | N/A | ~80ms | New feature |

## Key Features

### パフォーマンス
- **並列処理**: Task.async_streamによる並列リポジトリ処理
- **高速モード**: GitHub API呼び出しをスキップして80msで完了
- **並列度制御**: --max-concurrencyオプションで調整可能

### 開発品質
- **テストカバレッジ**: 15テスト（1 doctest + 14 unit tests）すべて合格
- **コード品質**: Credoで問題なし
- **型安全性**: Dialyzerで型エラーなし  
- **コードフォーマット**: mix formatで統一された形式

### 機能互換性
- 既存の全機能をサポート（コンパクト/詳細表示、フィルタリング）
- escriptとして \`ecosystem-manager\` コマンドでインストール
- Logger設定により通常時はwarningメッセージを非表示

## Technical Implementation

### アーキテクチャ
- **EcosystemManager**: メインAPI
- **EcosystemManager.CLI**: コマンドライン処理
- **EcosystemManager.Repository**: リポジトリ情報管理
- **EcosystemManager.GitHub**: GitHub API連携（並列処理）
- **EcosystemManager.Status**: ステータス表示処理

### 並列処理の仕組み
```elixir
Repository.all_repositories()
|> Enum.map(&Repository.new(&1, base_path))
|> Task.async_stream(&fetch_repository_info(&1, include_github),
                     max_concurrency: max_concurrency,
                     timeout: 15_000)
```

## Installation & Usage

```bash
# Install as escript
cd ecosystem_manager
mix escript.install

# Basic usage
ecosystem-manager                    # Show compact status
ecosystem-manager status --long     # Show detailed status  
ecosystem-manager status --fast     # Quick status (80ms)
ecosystem-manager --help           # Show help
```

## Development Tools Integration

All standard Elixir development tools are configured:

```bash
mix test                 # Run tests
mix credo               # Code quality analysis
mix dialyzer            # Type checking
mix format              # Code formatting
```

## Compatibility

- Elixir 1.18+
- 既存のecosystem-manager.shと完全互換
- 同じコマンドライン引数をサポート
- 出力形式も既存版と同一

## Test Plan

- [x] 基本機能テスト（status、help、各オプション）
- [x] パフォーマンステスト（高速モード・フルモード）
- [x] 品質チェック（test/credo/dialyzer/format）
- [x] インストールテスト（escript.install）
- [x] 互換性テスト（既存コマンドとの比較）

author: armru
body:
When the quality of service is set to "Guaranteed", CloudNativePG sets the `PG_OOM_ADJUST_VALUE` for the `postmaster` process to `0`.

This allows the `postmaster` to retain its low Out-Of-Memory (OOM) score of `-997`, while its child processes run with an OOM score adjustment of `0`. As a result, if the OOM killer is triggered, it will terminate the child processes before the `postmaster`.

This behaviour helps keep the PostgreSQL instance alive for as long as possible and enables a clean shutdown procedure in the event of an eviction.

Closes #7132

author: rastut
body:
### Description of the change

Fixes a bug in the Helm template condition that prevents the PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) from being rendered when using the `standalone` architecture.

The condition incorrectly references `.Values.primary.count`, which is not defined in the `values.yaml`. It has been updated to use `.Values.primary.replicaCount`, which is the correct and documented field for specifying the number of primary replicas.

### Benefits

Ensures that the PDB is rendered as expected when `primary.pdb.create` is `true` and `primary.replicaCount > 0`.

### Possible drawbacks

If any users were unknowingly relying on `primary.count` (despite it not being documented), their configuration might stop working. However, this is unlikely and would indicate misalignment with the intended values schema.
