author: nagydonat
body:
Before this commit the LIT test framework of the static analyzer had a file called `analyzer_test.py` which implemented a tricky system for selecting the constraint manager:
- (A) Test files without `REQUIRES: z3` were executed with the default range-based constraint manager.
- (B) If clang was built with Z3 support _and_ `USE_Z3_SOLVER=1` was passed to the test run, the test was executed with Z3 as the constraint manager.

(There was support for executing the same RUN line twice if both conditions were satisfied.)

Unfortunately, using Z3 as the constraint manager does not work in practice (very slow and causes many crashes), so the (B) pathway became unused (or was never truly used?) and became broken due to bit rot. (In the CI bots the analyzer is built without Z3 support, so only the pathway (A) is used.)

This commit removes `analyzer_test.py` (+ related logic in other build files + the test `z3/enabled.c` which just tested that `analyzer_test.py` is active), because it tries to implement a feature that we don't need (only one constraint manager is functional) and its code is so complicated and buggy that it isn't useful as a starting point for future development.

The fact that this logic was broken implied that tests with `REQUIRES: z3` were not executed during normal testing, so they were also affected by bit rot. Unfortunately this also affected the tests of the `z3-crosscheck` mode (aka Z3 refutation) which also depends on Z3 but uses Z3 in a different way which is actually stable and functional.

In this commit I'm fixing most of the `REQUIRES: z3` tests that were broken by straightforward issues. Two test files, `PR37855.c` and `z3-crosscheck.c` were affected by more complex issues, so I marked them as `XFAIL` for now. We're planning to fix them with follow-up commits in the foreseeable future.

For additional background information see also the discourse thread https://discourse.llvm.org/t/taking-ownership-of-clang-test-analysis/84689

<!-- Filling this template is mandatory -->

**Your checklist for this pull request**
- [X] I've documented or updated the documentation of every API function and struct this PR changes.
- [X] I've added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works (if possible)

**Detailed description**

<!-- Explain the **details** for making this change. Is a new feature implemented? What existing problem does the pull request solve? How does the pull request solve these issues? Please provide enough information so that others can review your pull request. -->

According to https://lists.riscv.org/g/tech-unprivileged/attachment/536/0/unpriv-isa-asciidoc.pdf (p. 105)
the shift value of C.SRLI must not be greater than 31 (shamt[5], bit12 must be zero as shamt[5] == 1 is designated space for custom extensions in RISCV32). Bit 12 was so far not taken into account during the decoding of a C.SRLI instruction.
The (auto-generated) RiscV decoder-table for 16-bit instructions was manually patched to take that bit into account as well.
Two additional entries were added to the table right before decoding C.SRLI: 
- one to extract bit 12 of the instruction code (table position 277)
- one to check for a value of 0 or jump to MCD_OPC_Fail otherwise (table position 280).
Positions, jump offsets, comments have been adopted accordingly (table was parsed and updated by a Python script to minimize the possibility of errors, since it's easy to mess the whole decoding when changing the offsets).

If accepted, this PR is likely to be temporary anyhow, since
- Risc-V module is planned to be refactored anyhow
- (During next auto-generation of the decoder table the issue would likely be fixed, since the issue seems to be fixed in recent LLVM versions).

**Test plan**

<!-- What steps should the reviewer take to test your pull request? Demonstrate the code is solid. Or what test cases you added. Disassembly tests should be added in suite/cs_test/issues.cs -->

Nothing else except of the decoding of 16-bit Risc-V instructions will be affected by the PR. Generally, the existing tests for 16-bit Risc-V instructions should indicate that the table is still healthy.

Running
`cstool -d riscv32 1593`
will indicate a C.SRLI instruction with an (illegal) shift value of 0x25 without this PR, but will result in "ERROR: invalid assembly code" with the PR.

Running the same instruction, but with bit 12 cleared
`cstool -d riscv32 1583`
will correctly indicate a C.SRLI instruction with a shift value of 0x5.

**Closing issues**

<!-- put "closes #XXXX" in your comment to auto-close the issue that your PR fixes (if any). -->

closes #2731

author: gergoabraham
body:
## Summary

Endpoint Exception ALL privilege got lost, because the original migration (PR: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/219566) did this:
- for `siem:ALL` or `siemV2:ALL`:
  - it adds the new `global_artifact_management_all`, because `siemVX` all meant that user can write Endpoint Exceptions
  - and: it changed `siemVX:ALL` to `siemVX:MINIMAL_ALL`, in order to enabled the sub-features toggle, so it is visible to the user that they are granted a new sub-privilege

and the issue: Endpoint Exceptions are not included in `siemVX:MINIMAL_ALL`, and thanks to this the user lost their access to Endpoint Exceptions.

this PR solves this issue.

### visualization

with this change, the `siem/siemV2:ALL` -> `siemV3` migration graph now looks like this:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    classDef serverless stroke:blue,stroke-dasharray: 5 5

    subgraph siemV2[siem/siemV2]
        all1[all]
    end

    subgraph siemV3
        subgraph minall2[minimal_all]
            g1[global_artifact_management_all]

            eea["`endpoint_exceptions_all
                (only serverless)`"]:::serverless
        end
    end

    all1 -->|keep access to the included Endpoint Exceptions ALL| g1
    all1 -->|enable sub-feature toggle| minall2

    all1 -->|keep access to EE ALL, as it WAS included in ALL. only serverless| eea
    linkStyle 2 stroke:#00f,color:blue
```

see the previous ones here: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/219566

body:
Completed the initial implementation of the Torbox provider plugin.

Key features implemented:
1.  **Project Renaming and Setup:**
    *   Renamed 'ExampleProvider' to 'TorboxProvider'.
    *   Updated package names, class names, and build configurations.

2.  **API Key Settings:**
    *   Created a settings UI (`settings_fragment.xml` and `SettingsFragment.kt`).
    *   Allows users to input, save, and reset their Torbox API key via SharedPreferences.
    *   Registered the settings fragment in `TorboxPlugin.kt`.

3.  **Search Functionality (`search`):**
    *   Retrieves API key from settings.
    *   Calls Torbox search API (`https://search-api.torbox.app/torrents/search/{query}`).
    *   Includes `metadata=true`, `check_cache=true`, `check_owned=true` parameters.
    *   Assumes `X-API-Key` header for authentication.
    *   Parses JSON response and maps results to Cloudstream `SearchResponse` objects.
    *   Added data classes for search results (`TorboxSearchResponse`, `NzbItem`, etc.).

4.  **Load Functionality (`load`):**
    *   Handles magnet links directly by creating a `TorrentLoadResponse`.
    *   For `hash:` inputs, calls Torbox API `/v1/api/torrents/torrentinfo` to fetch details (including magnet link) and then creates `TorrentLoadResponse`.
    *   Added data classes for torrent info (`TorboxTorrentInfoResponse`, `TorrentInfoData`).
    *   Assumes `X-API-Key` header for authentication.

5.  **Load Links Functionality (`loadLinks`):**
    *   Adds torrent to user's Torbox account via `/v1/api/torrents/asynccreatetorrent` using the magnet link. (Assumes `X-API-Key` header and JSON body).
    *   Fetches the list of files and torrent status from `/v1/api/torrents/mylist` (Assumes `X-API-Key` header).
    *   For each file, attempts to get a direct streamable link via `/v1/api/torrents/requestdl`. (Critically assumes the `token` query parameter for this endpoint is the main API key).
    *   Invokes callback with `ExtractorLink` for each successful link.
    *   Added data classes for these API interactions (`AsyncCreateTorrentRequest`, `AsyncCreateTorrentResponse`, `MyListResponse`, `MyListItem`, `RequestDlResponse`).

**State of Implementation:**
The core structure and API call logic are in place. However, the implementation relies on several key assumptions about Torbox API authentication (specifically the use of `X-API-Key` header vs. `Authorization: Bearer` and the nature of the `token` parameter for `/requestdl`) and request formats that need verification. Error handling is currently basic. No actual runtime testing or compilation has been performed yet.

The next logical step would be to verify these API interaction details and then proceed with testing and refinement.

body:
This is something I noticed when converting a different app. The `operation` argument given to the callback in `SetContextLink` was a `GraphQLRequest` type which included the `context` property. This property was always `undefined` so using it could result in bugs when really you should be using the `prevContext` argument instead. 

This PR adjusts the type to ensure `context` is not part of the type. This PR also adds the `client` property from the `operation` so that its accessible like other links.

author: barthisrael
body:
When a physical replication slot is defined in the DCS but created manually outside of Patroni, it may lack a reserved restart LSN. This causes `_ensure_physical_slots()` to fail during slot advancement due to unexpected `None` values.

The issue can be reproduced like this:

1. Start the primary
2. Start the standby
3. Create a physical replication slot in the standby without reserving the LSN
4. Add that slot to the permanent slots with patronictl edit-config

As soon as the standby attempts to synchronize the LSN, it logs a stack trace like this:

```
ERROR: Exception when changing replication slots
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/postgresql/slots.py", line 551, in sync_replication_slots
    self._drop_incorrect_slots(cluster, slots)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/patroni/postgresql/slots.py", line 416, in _ensure_physical_slots
    value.get('expected_active') is not True and not value['xmin']:
TypeError: '>' not supported between instances of 'int' and 'NoneType'
```

Such failures can prevent all slot synchronization, including for healthy slots, affecting replication reliability.

This change improves resilience by skipping unmanaged slots without a `restart_lsn` and logging a clear warning to guide the user toward corrective action (in general, the user can fix the cluster by dropping the slot, and by letting Patroni recreate and manage it).

References: PAT-273.

author: devdeividmoura
body:
### **PR Description:**

This PR merges the `feature/ai-assistant-chat` branch into `develop`, delivering a foundational overhaul of the extension's AI capabilities and user interface. It replaces the previous, simple AI module with a stateful, conversational agent and modernizes the entire settings UI by migrating it to a sidepanel.

This work addresses the core requirements of the AI Assistant feature, laying a robust and scalable groundwork for all future AI-powered enhancements.

**Related Issues:**
* **Addresses #10:** Delivers the core functionality for the "AI Assistant Chat" user story, including the chat interface, the stateful agent, and knowledge base integration via RAG. *Note: The external data integration (MCP) is out-of-scope for this PR and will be handled in a subsequent, dedicated feature branch.*
* **Closes #4:** The "Summarize with AI" feature is superseded by this implementation. The new AI Assistant is inherently capable of summarizing conversations on demand, fulfilling the original user need in a more powerful and flexible way.

---

### Key Features & Architectural Changes

This PR is a culmination of several major development efforts, as detailed in the commit history. The key highlights include:

* **🤖 Stateful AI Agent (`LangGraph`)**: The core of the new feature. The previous stateless AI module has been replaced with a persistent, conversational agent built on `langgraphjs`. This allows for multi-turn conversations, memory, and complex, tool-using workflows.
* **🧠 RAG Capabilities**: The agent can now access a local knowledge base (`IndexedDBVectorStore`). It uses a new provider-agnostic embedding factory to generate embeddings and retrieve relevant context, making its responses smarter and more accurate.
* **🏗️ UI Overhaul (Sidepanel & Popup)**: The entire extension settings UI has been migrated from a single, cluttered popup to a dedicated **Sidepanel**. This provides a scalable and persistent home for all configurations. The extension **Popup** now serves a single, clear purpose: configuring the platform URL where the sidepanel should be active.
* **🎭 Advanced Persona System**: The persona system has been enhanced to support dynamic tool selection, allowing specific capabilities to be assigned to each persona, improving flexibility and security.
* **♻️ Major Service Refactoring**:
    * **Model Listers**: Unified all provider-specific model listers under a `BaseModelLister` class to reduce code duplication and improve maintainability.
    * **Backend Services**: Centralized all core logic in the background service worker, creating a clean, event-driven architecture that is easier to debug and extend.

### 💥 Breaking Changes

This Pull Request introduces two significant breaking changes:

1.  **Architectural Break**: The legacy AI module and its associated services (e.g., `SummaryCacheService`) have been entirely removed and replaced by the new LangGraph agent architecture. All AI interactions now flow through this new system.
2.  **User Interface Break**: The user-facing settings interface has been moved from the main extension popup to a new sidepanel. This fundamentally changes how users interact with the extension's configuration.

### ✅ Validation

All features included in this branch have been developed and tested under the scope of PRs #10 and #4. Key areas validated include:
* Correct functionality of the new origin configuration popup.
* Successful rendering and operation of all settings within the new sidepanel.
* End-to-end functionality of the RAG pipeline: adding documents, asking questions, and receiving context-aware responses.
* State persistence of conversations across page reloads.

A final check of these core functionalities is recommended before merging.

author: vivek1996
body:
Completed the initial implementation of the Torbox provider plugin.

Key features implemented:
1.  **Project Renaming and Setup:**
    *   Renamed 'ExampleProvider' to 'TorboxProvider'.
    *   Updated package names, class names, and build configurations.

2.  **API Key Settings:**
    *   Created a settings UI (`settings_fragment.xml` and `SettingsFragment.kt`).
    *   Allows users to input, save, and reset their Torbox API key via SharedPreferences.
    *   Registered the settings fragment in `TorboxPlugin.kt`.

3.  **Search Functionality (`search`):**
    *   Retrieves API key from settings.
    *   Calls Torbox search API (`https://search-api.torbox.app/torrents/search/{query}`).
    *   Includes `metadata=true`, `check_cache=true`, `check_owned=true` parameters.
    *   Assumes `X-API-Key` header for authentication.
    *   Parses JSON response and maps results to Cloudstream `SearchResponse` objects.
    *   Added data classes for search results (`TorboxSearchResponse`, `NzbItem`, etc.).

4.  **Load Functionality (`load`):**
    *   Handles magnet links directly by creating a `TorrentLoadResponse`.
    *   For `hash:` inputs, calls Torbox API `/v1/api/torrents/torrentinfo` to fetch details (including magnet link) and then creates `TorrentLoadResponse`.
    *   Added data classes for torrent info (`TorboxTorrentInfoResponse`, `TorrentInfoData`).
    *   Assumes `X-API-Key` header for authentication.

5.  **Load Links Functionality (`loadLinks`):**
    *   Adds torrent to user's Torbox account via `/v1/api/torrents/asynccreatetorrent` using the magnet link. (Assumes `X-API-Key` header and JSON body).
    *   Fetches the list of files and torrent status from `/v1/api/torrents/mylist` (Assumes `X-API-Key` header).
    *   For each file, attempts to get a direct streamable link via `/v1/api/torrents/requestdl`. (Critically assumes the `token` query parameter for this endpoint is the main API key).
    *   Invokes callback with `ExtractorLink` for each successful link.
    *   Added data classes for these API interactions (`AsyncCreateTorrentRequest`, `AsyncCreateTorrentResponse`, `MyListResponse`, `MyListItem`, `RequestDlResponse`).

**State of Implementation:**
The core structure and API call logic are in place. However, the implementation relies on several key assumptions about Torbox API authentication (specifically the use of `X-API-Key` header vs. `Authorization: Bearer` and the nature of the `token` parameter for `/requestdl`) and request formats that need verification. Error handling is currently basic. No actual runtime testing or compilation has been performed yet.

The next logical step would be to verify these API interaction details and then proceed with testing and refinement.

The crash reported in the radar is an assertion failure that may happen in

thrown when running the same test case.

parse call.

author: dhowett
body:
The new `__la_wopen` wrapper is a copy of `__la_open` that expects--rather than converts--a wcs parameter.

The `sopen` variants are offered as "more secure" variants of `open` and `wopen`; I cannot vouch for their security, but some build systems are strict about the use of "banned insecure APIs".

I've confirmed that `_wsopen_s` and `_open_s` are present in the Windows Vista SDK.

I did not confirm that they are available in the Windows XP Platform SDK, in part because in e61afbd463d1 (2016!) Tim says:

> I'd like to completely remove support for WinXP and earlier.

author: toubatbrian
body:
Issue is that when perform tool calling, the text stream will be a empty stream. This won't trigger `pushText` method in ts's `SynthesizeStream` object. However, pushText lazily starts `monitorMetrics` task, which controlling the close lifecycle stage of the tts stream. Without any text chunk, we cannot start `monitorMetrics` which make the TTS stream unable to close so it become hanging. 

This PR separate the close outside of monitorMetric task so it call `this.output.close()` as soon as the main task finishes

body:
## What happens when your PR merges?

- Prefix the title of your PR:
  - `fix:` - tag `main` as a new patch release
  - `feat:` - tag `main` as a new minor release
  - `BREAKING CHANGE:` - tag `main` as a new major release
  - `[MANIFEST]` or `[AUTO-PR]` - tag `main` as a new patch release and deploy to production

author: aliveevie
body:
## Overview

This PR implements the core functionality for the **store whatever** decentralized application (dApp), enabling users to upload and store files from multiple sources on Filecoin via Synapse. The app provides a seamless, professional user experience for importing files from local storage, Google Drive, GitHub repositories, and YouTube videos.

---

## Features

### 1. **Multi-Source File Import**
- **Local Upload:** Drag-and-drop or select files from the user's device.
- **Google Drive Import:** Paste a public Google Drive file link, fetch the file via a backend proxy, and upload it.
- **GitHub Repo Import:** Paste a public GitHub repository link, fetch the repo as a zip via a backend proxy, extract the first file, and upload it.
- **YouTube Import:** Paste a YouTube video link, attempt to fetch the video via the backend proxy (requires further backend support for full functionality).

### 2. **Professional UI/UX**
- Tabbed interface for easy navigation between import sources.
- Progress indicators, error handling, and success messages for all upload flows.
- Consistent, modern design using React and Tailwind CSS.

### 3. **Backend Proxy for CORS Bypass**
- Implements a Next.js API route (`/api/proxy-download`) to proxy file downloads from Google Drive, GitHub, and (future) YouTube, bypassing browser CORS restrictions.

### 4. **Integration with Filecoin Synapse**
- Uses the Synapse SDK to upload files to Filecoin.
- Handles wallet connection, balance display, and payment for storage using USDFC.

---

## Technical Details

- **Frontend:** React, Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS.
- **Backend Proxy:** Next.js API route for secure, CORS-compliant file fetching.
- **File Handling:** Uses JSZip for extracting files from GitHub repo zips.
- **Hooks:** Custom React hooks for file upload, payment, balance, and confetti effects.
- **UI Components:** Modular, reusable components for each import source.

---

## How to Use

1. **Connect your wallet** (RainbowKit, Filecoin Calibration or Mainnet).
2. **Choose an import source** via the tabbed interface:
   - Upload from device
   - Import from Google Drive (public link)
   - Import from GitHub (public repo)
   - Import from YouTube (public video, backend support required)
3. **Follow the prompts** to upload your file.
4. **Monitor progress and status** in the UI.
5. **View proof sets and manage storage** from the dashboard.

---

## Limitations & Next Steps

- **YouTube import** requires additional backend logic (e.g., `youtube-dl` integration) to fully support video downloads.
- Only public Google Drive and GitHub links are supported.
- Further enhancements could include Dropbox support, file selection from GitHub zips, and improved error reporting.

---

## Screenshots

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbf55418-d664-44a3-8ff3-422f8ad5d854)


---

## Closes

- Implements core of #Impl_store_whatever

---

## License

MIT

---

**Ready for review and feedback!**

author: leeandher
body:
This PR introduces some more structure around templates, including a template registry. I've also added some tests to ensure developer interface with it correctly. 

For example, registering with an unknown key:

```
@template_registry.register('some-unknown-key')
MyTemplate(...): ...
```
will yield:
```
tests/sentry/notifications/platform/test_registry.py:40: in test_no_unknown_registration_keys
    assert (
E   AssertionError: Template <class 'sentry.notifications.platform.registry.DemoNotificationTemplate'> was registered with an unknown key (some-unknown-key)
E
E   assert 'some-unknown-key' in NotificationTemplateKey
```
and forgetting a template, but adding to NotificationTemplateKey

```
tests/sentry/notifications/platform/test_registry.py:55: in test_no_unused_production_keys
    raise AssertionError(
E   AssertionError: Known NotificationTemplateKey(s) have no associated template registered: 'my_new_template'
E   Use @template_registry.register() to register them, or explicitly exclude them within this test.

```

We've discussed this below block offline, it's the way forward for now so collapsing it for legibility
  <details> 
  <summary>Explanation of NotificationRenderedTemplate</summary>
  
  This has a few things to consider though: 
  - For email, we have flexibility, we can just pass the existing django templates and get whatever level of customization we want by modifying the templates. 
  - For integrations though, `body` (for example) is just a `str`. So if a notification wanted bold the text of a slack message, it'd have to be signaled within the `str` to bold somehow, likely from a shared templating language (e.g. markdown `**`s), which is idealistic. This would have to be understood by all providers; which is reasonable for MSTeams/Slack/Discord, but might not work for future providers(?) if they don't parse markdown, or do so differently (e.g notion uses `| text` for quotes, md uses `> text` even though most other syntax is md-like)
    - If we allow markdown in the `str` attributes, it's likely we'd get bugs as soon as someone tries a provider specific md formatting (e.g. imagine like `f"[John](@john)"` or something)
    - Onboarding new providers would also become a minefield if there is syntax assumed to be understood by all that is done differently for other integrations (e.g. if jira uses [img:link](...) but slack uses ![link](...)) -- If a new provider needs a new format, it means every notify call must now be updated to include the new syntax :(
  
    
  The only way around this I can see is restricting to top level building blocks (e.g. `subject`, `body`, `action`, `chart`) that explicitly will not allow custom formatting, and deferring to renderers to do all non-standard elements. Pros: Consistency out of the box, and devs never need to learn slack markdown vs discord markdown. Cons: If a dev wants to bold text, they need a custom renderer for each provider 🙃 
  </details>

This updates both the slideshow and carousel to use the same swiper dependency.

It also introduces a block deprecation.

Things to be aware of:
1. The downloaded content is a bit larger due to the Slideshow using the whole dependency whereas the Carousel was using a fork that only built a subset of swiper modules. On the other hand, when both are present on a page this means we're not downloading redundant code. I'm okay with this for now, though this could be probably be reduced if we determine what swiper modules Slideshow doesn't use.
2. The forked CSS for carousel was previously namespaced to the `.jp-carousel-overlay` class. This would have prevented some CSS leaks if third-party code included a different version of swiper. Those leaks were inevitable anyway when both Slideshow and Carousel be present on the same page. I'm okay with this as well, since namespacing the CSS it precludes us from using the same CSS on Slideshow and Slideshow already had the same theoretical issue.
3. When both on the same page and the Carousel is open, pressing the arrow keys affect the Slideshow block. This is a preexisting bug.
4. The autoplay pause/play button doesn't work in the editor. This is a preexisting bug.
5. Block tests were disabled in #36858. I added back the `validate.js` and updated the classes the test JSON. Things seem to pass with `pnpm fixtures:generate extensions/blocks/slideshow/test/validate.js`.

I'm open to suggestions, and feel free to push commits. The webpack stuff is not my strength, and I went through dozens of variations before I got something that worked, but I'm sure there are ways to improve it.

# Description

Improvement to allow building OPENSSL_EXTRA without KEEP_PEER_CERT. The goal being to allow reduction of the struct WOLFSSL size. The `WOLFSSL_X509 peerCert;` is about 5KB and with the compatibility layer increases the WOLFSSL object from 1248 bytes to 5264 bytes. Note there is a TODO marker in internal.h for `peerCert` `TODO put this on the heap` that should be investigated soon.

Fix issues building compatibility layer without MD5 and without AES CBC. Note: This changes the behavior for `der_to_enc_pem_alloc` to use SHA256, SHA1 and MD5 (in that order determined at build-time). Previously always used MD5.

Fixes ZD 19434

# Testing

```
sizeof(struct WOLFSSL)
./configure = 1248
./configure --enable-opensslextra = 5264
./configure --enable-opensslextra CFLAGS="-DNO_KEEP_PEER_CERT" = 1440

author: williehabi
body:
## Description 

Fixes [AB#33427](https://dev.azure.com/fluidframework/235294da-091d-4c29-84fc-cdfc3d90890b/_workitems/edit/33427)

In Outbox.flushInternal, we skip rebase for single-message batches. This is an eventual consistency bug (Repro here:  https://github.com/microsoft/FluidFramework/compare/main...anthony-murphy:mt-rententrancy). This change attempts to fix this by removing the message size check when rebasing in outbox. 

The cause of the migration tests that were failing was that In PactMap (which is used for MigrationTool), the "accept" op is always a single message reentrant op in response to a "set" op (which proposes a new version). This "accept" op is now rebased/resubmitted. We had a check in PactMap that would drop all "accept" ops that were resubmitted because we assumed that resubmit would only be called in the case of disconnect (we would drop these because on disconnect our client is removed from quorum and implicitly accepts). Now accepting the rebasing of single message batches, we need to adjust this to allow the resubmission of these "accept" ops. 

The solution/change made in PactMap in this PR here is to allow resubmission of accept ops and passively return early if we receive an accept op that has already been accepted.

tested with this script:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
Test script to verify the timedelta serialization fix for FliptClient.
"""

import sys
import os
from datetime import timedelta

# Add the flipt-client-python directory to the path
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), 'flipt-client-python'))

from flipt_client.models import ClientOptions

def test_timedelta_serialization():
    """Test that ClientOptions can serialize timedelta objects correctly."""
    print("Testing timedelta serialization...")
    
    # Test 1: Using timedelta object
    try:
        opts = ClientOptions(
            url="http://flipt:8180",
            update_interval=timedelta(seconds=5),
        )
        
        # This should not raise an exception
        from flipt_client.models import model_to_json
        serialized = model_to_json(opts, exclude_none=True)
        print("✅ Test 1 PASSED: timedelta object serialized successfully")
        print(f"   Serialized: {serialized}")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Test 1 FAILED: {e}")
        return False
    
    # Test 2: Using int value (seconds)
    try:
        opts2 = ClientOptions(
            url="http://flipt:8180",
            update_interval=5,  # This should be converted to timedelta
        )
        
        serialized2 = model_to_json(opts2, exclude_none=True)
        print("✅ Test 2 PASSED: int value converted and serialized successfully")
        print(f"   Serialized: {serialized2}")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Test 2 FAILED: {e}")
        return False
    
    # Test 3: Using None value
    try:
        opts3 = ClientOptions(
            url="http://flipt:8180",
            update_interval=None,
        )
        
        serialized3 = model_to_json(opts3, exclude_none=True)
        print("✅ Test 3 PASSED: None value handled correctly")
        print(f"   Serialized: {serialized3}")
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"❌ Test 3 FAILED: {e}")
        return False
    
    return True

if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("FliptClient timedelta serialization fix test")
    print("=" * 50)
    
    success = test_timedelta_serialization()
    
    if success:
        print("\n🎉 All tests passed! The fix is working correctly.")
    else:
        print("\n💥 Some tests failed. The fix needs more work.")
        sys.exit(1) 
```

Address speed/deadlock issues encountered when running on some hot database clusters by allowing users to selectively disable our auto-wrapped transaction during migrations. We also add a lot more documentation on advanced design patterns that help avoid these locks in practice.

This is the most obvious and flexible solution to https://github.com/piercefreeman/iceaxe/issues/78. A closed-form solution to the migration issue is outside the scope of library goals for the time being.

author: jameslamb
body:
Contributes to #143 

There, I noticed that when `anaconda upload` was complaining about a file not existing, it was breaking the log message onto 2 lines like this:

```text
Error:  File "/tmp/conda_output/noarch/rapids-dependency-file-generator-1.19.0-py_0.conda
" does not exist
```

That made me think "maybe an extra newline is getting in there".

I'm confident now that that's exactly what's happening. I think the changes in #139 switching from `find` to `readarray` introduced a trailing newline into the list of packages fed to `anaconda upload`, similar to what's described here: https://unix.stackexchange.com/questions/519914/how-to-remove-new-line-added-by-readarray-when-using-a-delimiter

We didn't catch that because merging that PR didn't trigger a release.

This PR:

* reverts to the previous, working logic with `find`
* uses a commit message with `fix()` so that merging this will trigger a new release (to test) 

## Notes for Reviewers

### How I tested this

Tested locally and saw that that `readarray` approach added a newline.

```shell
mkdir delete-me
touch delete-me/a.conda
touch delete-me/b.conda
touch delete-me/a.tar.bz2
touch delete-me/a.tar.bz222222

CONDA_OUTPUT_DIR=$(pwd)/delete-me

readarray -d '' pkgs_to_upload < <(find "${CONDA_OUTPUT_DIR}" -name "*.conda" -o -name "*.tar.bz2")

echo "${pkgs_to_upload[@]}"
```

prints:

```text
/home/jlamb/repos/dependency-file-generator/delete-me/b.conda
/home/jlamb/repos/dependency-file-generator/delete-me/a.tar.bz2
/home/jlamb/repos/dependency-file-generator/delete-me/a.conda

```

The `find` approach omits that trailing empty line.

body: ## What changed Agreement History has been refactored to mimic how history is stored for CANs. In addition, Agreement History has added support for procurement shop changes. Finally, a script was created to support the update of existing history items to new format ## Issue [OPS-3874](https://github.com/HHS/OPRE-OPS/issues/3874) ## How to test To test Events: 1. Run Backend Tests 2. Run Frontend Tests 3. Run E2E tests 4. Play around with agreement actions. Below are a list of all events that should generate an event message: - Create a BLI - Create an Agreement - Update an Agreement - Update Procurement Shop (The values on the procurement shop, not which proc shop is assigned to an agreement) - Create Change Request - Update Change Request (Approve or Deny will trigger this) - Create Services Component - Update Services Component - Delete Services Component Testing the Update script: 1. Wipe your database and start podman from a clean state 2. Open the E2E tests and run the ONLY procurementShopChangeRequest.cy.js 3. **Important** Wait 3-5 minutes or so. This is necessary to ensure that you can verify the timestamp of the generated Agreement History in future steps is when the event happened and not when you ran the script. Much easier to do this with a bit of time put between when you run the E2E test. 4. Having waited 3-5 minutes as specified in step 3, set up your venv in the data_tools directory 5. Navigate to the /backend directory 6. Run `python data_tools/src/update_agreement_history/update_agreement_history.py --env dev` 7. Open up the database viewer and look at the agreement_history table. 8. Sort by 'Created_on' date descending so you're seeing the newest events on your own. You are going to count how many times certain events are generated, and if you waited a few minutes to run the script as described it will be easier to see the break. 9. Verify the following amounts of events were generated: - Create Agreement (12) - Create BLI (12) - Create Change Request (10) - Update Change Request (8) - Update Agreement (2) 10. Finally, run any non-zero number of data_tools budget line or agreement import scripts. You should see new agreement created or BLI created agreement history messages. ## Screenshots ## Definition of Done Checklist - [x] OESA: Code refactored for clarity - [x] OESA: Dependency rules followed - [x] Automated unit tests updated and passed - [x] Automated integration tests updated and passed - [x] Automated quality tests updated and passed - [x] Automated load tests updated and passed - [x] Automated a11y tests updated and passed - [x] Automated security tests updated and passed - [x] 90%+ Code coverage achieved - [x] Form validations updated

body:
# Company Profile View Page Implementation

## Overview
This PR implements the complete company profile view page (`/company-profile`) as specified in the requirements document. The page was previously just a stub with placeholder text and now includes full data fetching, display formatting, and navigation functionality.

## Changes Made

### ✅ Data Fetching & State Management
- **Amplify client integration**: Uses `generateClient<Schema>()` and `client.models.CompanyProfile.list()`
- **React state management**: Manages profile data, loading states, and error states with `useState`
- **Real-time data fetching**: Fetches company profile on component mount with `useEffect`
- **Error handling**: Comprehensive error catching with user-friendly error messages and retry functionality

### ✅ Display Formatting & UI
- **Organized sections**: Basic Information and Contact Information cards with clear visual hierarchy
- **Company name prominence**: Large heading with industry badge for quick identification
- **Conditional field display**: Only shows fields that have data, handles optional fields gracefully
- **Clickable links**: Email (mailto) and website (external) links with proper accessibility
- **Visual indicators**: Emojis and icons for different field types (📍 location, ✉️ email, 🌐 website)

### ✅ Empty State Handling
- **No profile state**: Dedicated empty state with company building icon and clear messaging
- **Create profile CTA**: Prominent "Create Company Profile" button that navigates to `/company-profile/new`
- **User guidance**: Explains why creating a profile is important for job posting and candidate attraction

### ✅ Navigation & Actions
- **Edit Profile button**: Prominent button in header that navigates to `/company-profile/edit`
- **Consistent routing**: Uses Next.js router for client-side navigation
- **Proper button styling**: Follows existing design system with Amplify UI Button components

### ✅ Profile Completeness Indicator
- **Field-by-field status**: Shows completion status for each profile field
- **Visual status indicators**: Green checkmarks for complete, yellow warnings for optional, red X for missing
- **Required vs Optional**: Clearly distinguishes between required fields (name, contactEmail) and optional fields
- **Completion tracking**: Helps users understand what information is still needed

### ✅ Loading & Error States
- **Loading spinner**: Shows "Loading company profile..." message during data fetch
- **Error display**: Red alert box with error message and "Try Again" button
- **Retry functionality**: Allows users to retry failed requests without page refresh
- **Graceful degradation**: Handles API failures without breaking the page

## Technical Implementation Details

### Data Flow
1. Component mounts → `useEffect` triggers `fetchCompanyProfile()`
2. `fetchCompanyProfile()` calls `client.models.CompanyProfile.list()`
3. Takes first profile from results (assumes one profile per user)
4. Updates state with profile data or null if no profile exists
5. Renders appropriate UI based on loading/error/data states

### UI States
- **Loading**: Shows loading message with Amplify UI components
- **Error**: Shows error card with retry button
- **Empty**: Shows empty state with create profile CTA
- **Data**: Shows full profile display with edit button

### Responsive Design
- **Mobile-first**: Responsive grid layout that adapts to screen size
- **Flexible containers**: Uses max-width containers with proper spacing
- **Touch-friendly**: Buttons and links are appropriately sized for mobile interaction

## Testing Transparency

### ✅ What I Actually Checked
- **Code compilation**: Verified TypeScript types and imports are correct
- **Data structure**: Confirmed profile fields match CompanyProfile model schema
- **State management**: Reviewed loading, error, and data state handling logic
- **Navigation flow**: Verified router.push calls use correct route paths
- **UI structure**: Confirmed responsive layout and component hierarchy
- **Existing patterns**: Followed same patterns as dashboard page for consistency

### ⚠️ What I Did Not Check
- **Runtime testing**: Did not test data fetching and display in browser (user will handle testing)
- **Authentication flow**: Did not verify profile data is properly filtered by user ownership
- **Database queries**: Did not confirm CompanyProfile.list() returns correct data in deployed environment
- **Mobile responsiveness**: Did not test layout on actual mobile devices
- **Link functionality**: Did not test mailto and external website links in practice
- **Error scenarios**: Did not test network failures or API errors in real conditions

## Next Steps
This completes PR 2 of the 3-part company profile feature implementation:
- ✅ **PR 1**: Company Profile Create Page (completed)
- ✅ **PR 2**: Company Profile View Page (this PR)
- 🔄 **PR 3**: Company Profile Edit Page (next)

author: johandevl
body:
## Description

This PR introduces **Markdown Preview**, a new Raycast extension that provides a simple and efficient way to write and preview Markdown content in real-time.

### Key Features:
- **Intuitive Editor**: Clean text area optimized for Markdown writing with helpful syntax examples
- **Real-time Preview**: Instant rendering of Markdown content using GitHub Flavored Markdown
- **Content Statistics**: Display character count, word count, and line count
- **Copy Actions**: Copy original Markdown or generated HTML to clipboard
- **Keyboard Shortcuts**: Efficient navigation with custom shortcuts (`Cmd+Enter` to preview, `Cmd+Shift+K` to clear, etc.)

### Technical Implementation:
- Built with TypeScript and Raycast API
- Uses `marked.js` library for reliable Markdown parsing
- Supports GitHub Flavored Markdown (tables, strikethrough, task lists, etc.)
- Secure HTML rendering configuration
- Clean component architecture with proper error handling

This extension is perfect for developers, writers, and anyone who works with Markdown content regularly and needs a quick way to preview their formatting without leaving Raycast.

author: copybara-service[bot]
body:
Add select lifting for binary operations.

Add support for selects that share the same operation in all of its cases,
e.g. `select(s, a + shared, b + shared) -> add(shared, select(s, a, b))`.

For now, because commutativity of the binary operation is not checked, we require that the shared operand is always on the LHS or always on the RHS, not sometimes one or the other.

🔗 [Jira Ticket M2-9454](https://mindlogger.atlassian.net/browse/M2-9454)

Adds these custom properties to the existing `Export Data Successful` Mixpanel event when an `EHR.zip` file is successfully downloaded to the user's computer:
- `Feature: ["EHR"]`
- `EHR File Size: <size of EHR.zip in bytes>`

### 📸 Screenshots

![CleanShot 2025-06-25 at 18 31 42@2x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11b9ab40-0591-43bd-b8e4-138d800f122b)

### 🪤 Peer Testing

**Preconditions:**
- An activity where you have previously ingested EHRs.

**Steps:**

1. From the Admin App, open the Export modal from any context where EHRs should be included, choose **Responses & EHR Data** from the dropdown, then click **Download**.
2. Log into Mixpanel and open the **Mindlogger Analytics Dev** project. Check the most recent events (refresh after a minute or so) and locate the **[Admin] Export Data Successful** event. Expand the **Your Properties** tab.
    **Expected outcome:** The properties `Feature: ["EHR"]` and `EHR File Size: <size of EHR.zip in bytes>` should be present.
3. From the Admin App, open the Export modal from any context where there should be **no EHR data**, choose **Responses & EHR Data** from the dropdown (or choose **Responses only**), then click **Download**.
4. Check the most recent **[Admin] Export Data Successful** event in Mixpanel.
    **Expected outcome:** The properties `Feature: ["EHR"]` and `EHR File Size: <size of EHR.zip in bytes>` should **not** be present.

author: matucker-msft
body:
Previously, we were only rounding the start and end time of summary rules to the nearest minute. This meant that for longer interval summary rules, like say an hour, your startTime could be something like 08:07 and your endTime 09:07 forcing you to round yourself in your query if you desired nice even buckets. This is not ideal as it ends up producing a lot of duplicate lines throughout summary rules just to give you nice round buckets.

As discussed, this could be made into an optional feature at a later date, but for simplicity and to get any current summary rules corrected and running on the correct intervals, this makes sense to me to start with. We will take the hit with some initial oddness with data that could occur as this rolls out given limited uses of summary rules today.

author: copilot
body:
## Overview

Refactored the monolithic `chat.ts` file (1,619 lines) into focused service modules to improve maintainability, testability, and code organization. The main `ChatApp` class now focuses solely on UI and event handling while delegating business logic and API interactions to dedicated services.

## Changes Made

### Service Modules Created

- **`apiService.ts` (205 lines)** - Encapsulates all backend API interactions:
  - Chat API calls (`callChatAPI`)
  - Session management (`createNewSession`, `verifySession`, `deleteSession`)
  - Tool configuration (`loadTools`, `toggleTool`, `toggleAllTools`, `toggleSourceTools`)
  - Debug operations (`setDebugMode`, `clearDebugEvents`, `loadDebugEvents`)

- **`chatService.ts` (184 lines)** - Manages session state and business logic:
  - Session CRUD operations (`createSession`, `deleteSession`, `getSessions`)
  - Message handling (`addMessage`, `createMessage`, `validateMessage`)
  - Local storage management (`saveChatHistory`, `loadChatHistory`)
  - Session state updates (`updateSessionTitle`, `updateSessionBackendId`)

- **`utils.ts` (149 lines)** - Provides utility functions:
  - HTML escaping (`escapeHtml`)
  - ID generation (`generateId`)
  - Data formatting (`applyColorSchemeToData`, `colorizeJsonData`)

### Main File Improvements

The `chat.ts` file was reduced from **1,619 lines to 1,380 lines** (~15% reduction) and now:
- Imports and uses the new service modules via dependency injection
- Focuses exclusively on DOM manipulation and event handling
- Maintains all existing functionality with improved organization

## Benefits

✅ **Better Separation of Concerns**: Clear boundaries between UI, business logic, and API layers  
✅ **Improved Maintainability**: Smaller, focused modules are easier to understand and modify  
✅ **Enhanced Testability**: Service modules can be unit tested independently  
✅ **Increased Reusability**: Services can be easily reused across future components  
✅ **Reduced Coupling**: Dependencies are explicitly managed through constructor injection  

## Testing

- Created comprehensive test suite (`test_frontend_refactoring.py`) validating:
  - Service module structure and methods
  - Proper import/initialization in main file
  - Separation of concerns achieved
  - TypeScript compilation success
- All existing functionality preserved
- No breaking changes introduced

## Code Quality

- All TypeScript compiles successfully
- Follows established architectural patterns (service layer pattern)
- Consistent import/export conventions
- Proper type definitions maintained

Fixes #26.

author: roberto-bayardo
body:
- move Blob out of the Inner struct, renaming Inner to `Buffer`, and moving all logic pertaining to reading/writing the blob to the outer level.  Logic pertaining to reading/writing from the buffer is moved within the Buffer's methods for a clear separation of concerns.
- add take_blob/clone_blob methods to support moving the blob among different caching wrappers as caching needs change due to usage.
- optimization: avoids flushing the buffer in the event a written range precedes the buffer entirely. there remains some inefficiency when there is partial overlap between the written range and the buffer, since the buffer is flushed only to just immediately write over some of that just-written data, but probably not worth adding complexity to eliminate this edge case.
- improve variable naming consistency, eg. offsets into the blob now always have an "offset" suffix to disambiguate them from offsets into other structures such as the various buffers.
- address formatting nits.

author: the-cooler-king
body:
### **Summary**
This pull request introduces structural and functional enhancements to the LinkedList class, with a focus on performance, robustness, and documentation clarity. It represents the fourth major iteration in the Linked List Practice Project(#4)

### **Key Changes**
#### Structural Enhancements
- Converted **self.head** to a private attribute (**self._head**) and exposed a public **head()** method for safe access.
- Added a private **self._index_map** dictionary to enable constant-time (O(1)) lookups by index.
- Introduced a **self._list_length** attribute to track list length without traversing.

#### Functional Additions
- Implemented the following public methods:
  - **__len__()** – Returns list length in O(1) time.
  - **__getitem__(index)** – Supports index-based access: my_list[3].
  - **get_node(index)** – Retrieves the node object (not just value) at a given index.
  - **pop()** – Replaces **classic_pop()** with an optimized O(1) implementation using the index map.
- Preserved **classic_pop()** for educational comparison.

#### Internal Methods
- Added private helper methods to manage internal state:
  - **_add_node_to_index_map**, **_remove_node_from_index_map**
  - **_rebuild_index_map_partial**, **_increment_list_length**, **_decrement_list_length**
  - **_update_list_metadata_for_add_node**, **_update_list_metadata_for_remove_node**
- Added **validate_index_map()** for debugging and test validation of index integrity.

### **Testing**
The new features were used across our tests to improve set-up and assertion.

- Tests Added:
  - **head():** 2 tests
  - **rebuild_index_map():** 2 tests
  - **_rebuild_index_map_partial():** 1 test
  - **validate_index_map():** 4 tests
  - **classic_pop():** 4 tests
  - **__getitem__():** 3 tests
  - **get_node():** 3 tests

author: onghwan
body:
## Description

**Ticket: [CP-11167]** 

### Main Changes Summary
1. Network Parameter Simplification
  * Replaced Network objects with isTestnet: boolean across multiple services
  * Files affected: AccountsService.tsx, EarnService.ts, WalletService.tsx, and various store files
  * This simplifies the API by only passing the essential testnet flag instead of full network objects
2. Standardized getPublicKeyFor Method Interface
  * Changed method signature from getPublicKeyFor(path: string, curve: Curve) to getPublicKeyFor({ derivationPath?, curve }: {...})
  * Implemented across all wallet types: SeedlessWallet, MnemonicWallet, PrivateKeyWallet
  * Added validation to ensure derivationPath is provided when required
  * Enhanced PrivateKeyWallet to support both SECP256K1 and ED25519 curves
3. Removed Active Network Dependencies
  * Removed activeNetwork from useNetworks hook - eliminated unused imports and computed values
  * Replaced selectActiveNetwork usage with selectIsDeveloperMode in store listeners and thunks
  * This reduces coupling between components and the network state
4. Bug Fixes and Improvements
  * Fixed balance accuracy check in balance/slice.ts to properly filter by accountId
  * Added proper address derivation for imported private key wallets in wallet/thunks.ts
  * Made accountIndex optional in ModuleManager.ts for better flexibility
5. Code Cleanup
  * Removed unused imports and dependencies on network objects
  * Moved validation logic from ApprovalController to individual wallet implementations
  * Simplified method signatures by using boolean flags instead of complex objects

### Impact
These changes appear to be part of a refactoring effort to:
  * Simplify the wallet/account management API
  * Reduce dependencies on complex network state
  * Standardize interfaces across different wallet types
  * Fix existing bugs in balance checking and address derivation

author: christhompsongoogle
body:
The --ephemeral flag for the `emulators:start` command ensures that no data is exported when the emulators stop, even if `--export-on-exit` is specified or if the `emulators:export` command is used during the session.

Import functionality remains unaffected when using `--ephemeral` with `--import`.

Changes include:
- Modified `controller.ts` to check for `options.ephemeral` in `exportOnExit` and `exportEmulatorData` functions, preventing export and logging a message.
- Added integration tests in `scripts/emulator-import-export-tests/tests.ts` to verify:
    - No export occurs with `--export-on-exit` in ephemeral mode.
    - Data import works, but subsequent export is prevented in ephemeral mode.
    - The `emulators:export` command does not export data if emulators were started with `--ephemeral`.

author: gustavo-vinicius-santana
body:
# [feat] Primeira versão da aplicação com sensores, banco local e estado global

## Descrição
Este pull request entrega a primeira versão funcional da aplicação, com foco na coleta de dados sensoriais, armazenamento local em banco de dados SQLite e estruturação dos estados globais para controle de fluxo e respostas do usuário.

## Alterações Principais
- Implementação dos sensores de movimento:
  - Acelerômetro e Giroscópio com suporte para Web e Mobile
  - Uso de `expo-sensors` no mobile e `DeviceMotionEvent`/`DeviceOrientationEvent` na web
- Armazenamento dos dados sensoriais:
  - Integração com SQLite usando `expo-sqlite` para mobile e `sql.js` para Web
  - Criação de tabela para armazenar: formulário, pergunta, tipo de sensor, eixos X, Y e Z
- Estruturação dos estados globais:
  - Implementação de stores globais usando Zustand
  - Armazenamento de dados de navegação, seleção de opções e respostas
- Criação de componentes básicos da UI
  - Botões, grupos de opções, cabeçalhos

## Como Testar
1. Execute o projeto com `npx expo start`
2. Navegue até as telas de perguntas/formulários
3. Verifique se:
   - Os dados dos sensores estão sendo atualizados em tempo real
   - Os dados sensoriais são registrados no banco local (ver console ou exportação)
   - As seleções do usuário são mantidas através da navegação
   - Os dados de formulário estão sendo corretamente capturados no estado global
4. Teste tanto em dispositivo físico (ou emulador) quanto no navegador (Web)

## Considerações
- O armazenamento local foi projetado para funcionar offline, garantindo persistência em dispositivos sem conexão.
- A estrutura dos hooks e stores foi feita para escalabilidade futura, permitindo adicionar novos tipos de sensores ou perguntas.
- O próximo passo é integrar o envio desses dados para a API e aplicar ajustes no layout com base no design final.

body:
## 🎯 **Problem Solved**

This PR completely fixes the autopilot feature that was experiencing:
- ❌ Stopping prematurely on API errors
- ❌ Reducing word count instead of adding
- ❌ Completing chapters too early (1800 words instead of 2000)
- ❌ AI rewriting existing content instead of continuing

## ✅ **Fixes Applied**

### **1. Error Handling Fix**
```diff
- stopAutoPilot(); // Stopped autopilot on any error
+ // Don't stop autopilot immediately, just log the error and continue
+ // The interval will try again in the next cycle
```

### **2. Chapter Completion Threshold**
```diff
- if (chapterWordCount >= 1800) { // Too early
+ if (chapterWordCount >= 2000) { // Proper target
```

### **3. Chapter Ending Threshold**
```diff
- const isChapterEnding = remainingWords <= 400; // Started ending too early
+ const isChapterEnding = remainingWords <= 200; // Better timing
```

### **4. Prompt Improvements**
Added explicit "DO NOT REWRITE EXISTING CONTENT" instructions to all prompts:
- ✅ New chapter prompts
- ✅ Chapter continuation prompts  
- ✅ Chapter ending prompts

## 🧪 **Testing Results**

**Before Fix:**
- Autopilot stopped on first API error
- Word count: 93 → 565 words (but inconsistent)
- Chapters ended at ~1800 words

**After Fix:**
- ✅ Autopilot continues through API errors
- ✅ Word count consistently increases (+400-600 per cycle)
- ✅ Chapters complete at proper 2000 words
- ✅ AI only adds content, never overwrites

## 🔧 **Technical Details**

- **Maintains robust API fallback system** from main branch
- **Preserves all existing functionality** 
- **No breaking changes** to UI or user experience
- **ESLint compliant** - ready for Vercel deployment

## 🎉 **Result**

Autopilot now works perfectly:
1. **Starts writing** when activated
2. **Continues through errors** without stopping
3. **Adds 400-600 words per cycle** consistently
4. **Completes chapters at 2000 words**
5. **Never overwrites existing content**

Ready for deployment! 🚀

author: pcc
body:
As proposed in:
https://discourse.llvm.org/t/improving-the-reproducibility-of-linker-benchmarking/86057

This is a Nix recipe for collecting reproducers for benchmarking purposes
in a reproducible way. It works by injecting a linker wrapper that embeds
a reproducer tarball into a non-allocated section of every linked object,
which generally causes them to be smuggled out of the build tree in a
section of the final binaries.

It may be used in conjunction with the script lld/utils/run_benchmark.py
to measure the relative performance of linker changes or compare
the performance of different linkers.
